There, my eye has seen everything, my ear has heard and understood it;
I too know the same things you know, am not inferior to you.
But I am speaking to Shaddai and would like to argue with Deity.
But you are whitewashers, quack doctors all of you.
Would that you would hold your tongues so that it should become wisdom for you!
Hear out my argument and listen to the contentions of my lips!
Will you talk unfairly for Deity and stream out fraud for him?
Will you be partial to his side, or champion Deity’s cause?
Is it a good thing that he should investigate you, or would you hoax him as one hoaxes a man?
He will be calling you to account if you show private partiality.
Should not his majesty overwhelm you and the dread of him fall upon you?
Your memorable sayings are proverbs of ashes, your shield-bosses turn out to be crockery.
Be still, and I will do the talking, come what may.
I will pick up my flesh in my teeth, take my life in my hand.
Suppose he slays me: I will not wait, I will just argue my course to his face.
He will become salvation to me too, because an ungodly man will not be admitted before him.
Hear my word, do, and take my demonstration into your ears.
Here I have formulated my case: I know I am the one that will turn out to be in the right.
Who will join issue with me? for I would now hold my tongue and pass away.
Only do not do two things with me, then I will not screen myself from your face:
Take your hand away from me and let your terror not overwhelm me,
And call, and I will answer; or I will speak, and return me a reply.
How much of guilts and sins do I have? let me know my crime and sin.
Why do you veil your face from me and count me as an enemy of yours?
Would you terrorize a driven leaf or chase dry straw,
That you list bitter things against me and saddle me with the guilts of my boyhood
And set my feet in the stocks, and watch all my paths, and mark a line round the soles of my feet—
And he is like a worn-out water-bag, like a moth-eaten blanket.
“Man, the woman-born, has a scanty lifetime and an overload of difficulties.
Like a flower he came out and wilted, fled away like a shadow and does not stand.
Upon even this you open your eyes and summon him to appear against you for trial!
Who shall produce a clean thing out of unclean? not one.
If his time is decided, you have his number of months, you have drawn his bounds and he is not to go beyond,
Glance away from him and leave off till, like a hired man, he takes the satisfaction of his day.
For there is hope for a tree: if it is cut down, it starts again, and its shoot will not fail to come;
If its root grows old in the ground and its trunk dies in the soil,
At the scent of water it will sprout and make a twig like a young tree newly set.
But a man dies and lies lifeless; a human being breathes his last, and where is he?
Water goes away from a sea and a river dries off and out,
And a man lies down and will not get up; till the sky wears out they will not wake nor rouse from their sleep.
O that you would stow me away in the world below, screen me till your anger turned back, fix a date for me and remember me!
If a man dies will he come to life? I would wait all the time I had to serve till my relief came;
You would call and I would answer you; you would have a yearning for the work of your hands.
For then you would be counting my steps, not watching for my sin,
My crime would be packed up under seal, and you would whitewash my guilt.
“But a mountain tumbles down, wears out, and a rock shifts from its place;
Water pulverizes stones; a cloudburst washes away soil; and you have crushed man’s hope.
You force him permanently out, and he goes; you change his face and turn him off.
His sons rise to honor and he does not know it, or sink into insignificance and he does not find out about them;
Only his flesh feels pain upon himself and his soul is mournful over himself.”
And Eliphaz the Temanite answered
“Would a wise man answer with windy ideas and fill himself up with east wind,
Arguing with unserviceable talk and useless phrases?
You, besides, are breaking up fear of the Deity and lessening thoughtfulness before him,
Because your guilt is tutoring your mouth and you choose artful men’s language.
Your own mouth shall prove you in the wrong, not I, and your own lips shall testify against you.
Are you the first of men to be born? were you brought forth before the hills?
Did you listen into God’s private conference and sequester some wisdom for yourself?
What do you know that we do not, perceive that we are not aware of?
We have among us graybeard and patriarch, further on in years than your father.
Are Deity’s consolations too little for you, and talk that is easy on you?
Why does your heart carry you away, and what do your eyes fasten on,
That you send your breath back to Deity and pour phrases out of your mouth?
What is man that he should be pure and that one born of woman should be in the right?
Here, he does not put trust in his holy ones and sky is not pure to his eyes,
To say nothing of an abominable and degenerate being, a man who drinks rascality like water.
“I will show you; give me a hearing; I have recognized this and will tell you about it,
What wise men state and their fathers have not kept back.
They had the country given to them alone, and no stranger came through among them.
All a wrong-doer’s life he is in expectation, the number of years that are laid up for the violent man.
Sounds of dread are in his ears, in peace there is a ravager coming to him;
He does not count on coming back out of darkness, and he is marked for the sword;
He has an appointment to be a meal for a kite; he knows his disaster is a settled thing;
A day of darkness will overwhelm him, distress and hard straits will overpower him, like a king ready for the onslaught,
Because he stretched out his hand against Deity and blustered against Shaddai,
Running at him headlong with thick shield-fronts.
Because he covered his face with fat and put on flesh in his waist,
And planted himself in extirpated cities, houses that were never to be lived in, which had been made ready to become heaps of stones,
His means shall not be rich, shall not grow up to stalks, shall not bend ears earthward;
He shall not get out of darkness; flame shall dry up his shoot, and his buds shall blow off in the wind;
Let him not trust to rambling futility, for futility will be his purchase;
His fronds shall wither untimely and his new fronds not grow verdant;
He shall blast his berries like a grapevine and drop his blossoms like an olive-tree.
For a godless man’s company is stony ground, and fire has devoured the tents of bribery;
There is breeding of trouble and giving birth to villainy, and inside them fraud is shaping up.”
But Job answered
“I have heard plenty like that; you are plaguy comforters all of you.
Is there any end to windy talk? or what is galling you, that you answer?
I too might speak as you do if your souls were in the place of mine; I might string phrases together about you and shake my head over you;
I might brace you up with my mouth, and the comfort of my lips might check—
If I speak my pain is not checked, and if I refrain what passes away from me?
He has just tired me out now; you have laid all my company desolate,
And you have gripped me, it has become a witness, and my leanness stands up against me, testifies to my face.
His anger tore me and flung me down; he ground his teeth at me; my foe sharpens his eyes for me.
They have opened their mouths at me, insolently struck my cheeks, collected in full force against me.
The Deity gives me up to a foul-player and thrusts me into the hands of wrong-doers.
I was in quietness and he jerked me, took me by the back of my neck and burst me, And sets me up for his target,
his marksmen surround me, And he cuts through my kidneys unsparingly, lets my gall run out on the ground,
Wounds me with wound across wound, runs at me like a warrior.
I have stitched a sackcloth on my hide and run my horn into the clay,
My face is inflamed with weeping and there is gloom over my eyelashes,—
For no violence that I have on my hands; and my prayer is pure.
Earth, do not cover my blood, and let there be no place for my outcry!
Even now my witness is there, in the heavens, and I have my voucher aloft,
My friend is my interpreter; to God my eye drips,
That he would arbitrate for a man with a God and between a human being and his fellow.
For a few years are to come and I shall go on the track I shall not come back on.
My spirit is blighted, my days are snuffed out, graves are mine.
Decidedly I have triflers about me and my eyes grow tired resting on their ungovernableness.
Give yourself bail for me; who would there be to strike into my hand?
For you have kept their hearts closeted from sense; therefore you will not set them on high.
He notifies friends for a share, and his sons’ eyes are worn out with looking and longing.
But you have set me up for a byword of peoples, and I am a phenomenon before them,
And my eyes are dim with vexation and my figure dissolves like a shadow.
Upright men will stand aghast at this, and an innocent man be stirred up against an ungodly;
But a right-doer will hold his course and a cleanhanded man grow increasingly resolute.
But you may all come again and I shall not find a wise man among you.
My days have gone past; I am annihilated; my heartstrings are snapped.
They make night into day, ‘light is near, coming away from darkness.’
If I hope, the realm of death is my house; I have made up my couch in the darkness;
I have called decay my father, the maggot my mother and sister,—
And where is hope of mine? and who is to behold good fortune of mine?
Will they go down with me to the realm of death? or shall we go underground together?”
And Bildad the Shuhite answered
“How long will you be snaring phrases? See the point, and afterward we may talk.
How comes it we seem like cattle to your eyes,
you that tear yourself in your anger? Is earth to be forsaken on your account, and a rock shifted from its place?
A wrong-doer’s light does go out, and the blaze of his fire gives no radiance.
Light turns dark in his tent, and his lamp goes out over him.
His vigorous steps will be cramped and his own purposes will upset him,
For he runs his feet into a net and walks along on wickerwork.
A trap will grip his heel and a noose clutch him.
The cord for him is hidden on the earth and the snare for him along the path.
On all sides wraiths overwhelm him and chevy him wherever he goes.
His vigor is famished and calamity stands ready for his weakening.
His skin is eaten away by disease; the firstborn of death eats his members.
He is torn out of his tent, what he trusted to, and is marched to the king of wraiths.
There shall be living in his tent something that is not his; brimstone shall be sprinkled over his lands.
His roots shall die out underneath and his twigs wither overhead.
The memory of him is lost from earth and there is no name of his over the wide world.
He is pushed out of light into darkness and sent flitting out of the world.
He has neither chick nor child among his people nor any survivor in the places he has visited.
Over the day that comes for him men of the west shall stand aghast and men of the east be taken with a shudder.
Altogether such are the dwellings of a malefactor, and like this is the place of one who knows not Deity.”
But Job answered
“How long will you make my soul miserable and beat me down with phrases?
This is ten times you have been humiliating me, you are not embarrassed to keep saying spiteful things about me.
But even take it that I really have made a misstep: it is with me my misstep is lodged.
If you are really taking high ground with me and proving my ignominy against me,
Know that it is God has done the unfair thing by me and set his toils round me.
Suppose I cry murder, I am not answered; I shout an appeal and there is no administration of justice.
He has walled off my road and I cannot pass; he has spread darkness over my paths.
He has stripped my honor off me and taken away the crown from my head.
He tears down every side of me, and I am gone, and he has cleared away my hope like a piece of timber.
He is angry with me and thinks of me as he does of his foes.
His raiders come on unitedly and have built their road against me and are camped round my tent.
He has set my brothers to standing aloof from me, and my acquaintances are altogether estranged from me.
My nearest and dearest have quit, my housemates have forgotten me,
And my serving-maids think me a stranger, I seem to them a foreigner.
I have called my slave and he does not answer— I beg him for favors with my own mouth.
My breath is hateful to my wife and I smell foul to the sons of my body.
Even children think nothing of me; let me stand up, they talk at me.
All my bosom friends abhor me, and whom I loved have turned on me.
My bones stick to my skin, and I come off with my flesh in my teeth.
Be kind to me, be kind to me, you friends of mine, because God’s hand has touched me.
Why is it you chase me down as Deity does and can never get enough of my flesh?
O that what I have to say were written down, were registered in a document,
With iron pen and lead, carved in rock forevermore!
But as for me, I know my vindicator is alive, and one in future will stand up above ground,
And behind my skin, which has borne this, out of my flesh I shall behold God,
Whom I shall behold for myself; it will be my eyes that saw, and not a stranger— my heart is spent in my bosom!
When you think ‘What of his shall we chase down and find ground for a case in him?’
Quail on your own account for fear of a sword, because those are offenses to bring down the sword, so that you may know there is an arbiter.”
And Sophar the Naʽamathite answered
“For that my thoughts give me response, and by reason of it I am hurried on.
I hear a tutoring that humiliates me and wind rather than sense answers me—
Have you known this from of yore, since man was set on earth?
For wrong-doers’ caroling is shortsighted, and an ungodly man’s merrymaking is momentary.
If he lifts his crest to the sky and his head touches the cloud,
Like his dung he perishes utterly; those who saw him say ‘Where is he?’
Like a dream he takes wing and one cannot find him; he flits away like a vision of the night.
An eye has glimpsed him, but does so no more, and his place will not behold him again.
His sons must give satisfaction to poor men, his hands give back his goods.
His bones are full of his virility, but with him it lies down in the clay.
If evil is sweet in his mouth, he hides it under his tongue,
Saves it up, will not let go of it, keeps it snug in the roof of his mouth,
His dinner turns in his bowels, he has vipers’ gall within him,
He has swallowed wealth but must throw it up, Deity ousts it from his stomach.
He sucks vipers’ poison, a sand-adder’s tongue will kill him.
He must never look on outflows of oil, streams of honey and clabber.
Because of old age he will not swallow what he has spent his strength on, he will not be gay in proportion to the wealth he has traded for,
Because he victimized and abandoned poor men, stole a house, and does no building on it.
Because he had no quiet in his stomach, in his wishes he let nothing get away,
There was nothing left over from his eating, therefore his good time will not persist.
In his full plenty let him come into distress, all the force of trouble come over him.
Let him have his bellyful, let Him turn His anger loose on him and shower it on him into his entrails.
He takes flight from arms of iron; a bow of bronze drives through him;
He pulls and it comes out of his back, comes flashing away from his gall. Terrors are upon him;
all darkness lurks for him. Let an unblown fire consume him, feed on survivors in his tent;
Let the heavens uncover his guilt and earth be an adversary to him;
Let the progeny of his house be swept out of the country, drifted wreckage on the day of His anger.
This is a wicked man’s lot from God, and the estate named for him by Deity.”
But Job answered
“Do hear what I have to say, and let this be your comforting.
Bear me, and I myself will speak; and after I speak you shall make your fun.
Is my grievance against man? and how should I not be impatient?
Face toward me and stand aghast and lay your hands over your mouths!
And if I bethink myself I am in consternation, and a shudder seizes my flesh.
How comes it that wrong-doers live, come to advanced age and are still notably robust?
Their posterity is firmly established before them; their offspring is numerous under their eyes.
Their houses are at peace from dread, and God’s cudgel is not on them.
His bull covers and does not miss, his cow calves and does not slink.
They let out their brats like sheep and goats, and their children caper about.
They sing with tambourine and lyre and make merry to the sound of the pipe.
They wear out their days in comfort, and all of a sudden they go down to the world below.
And they have said to the Deity ‘Get out of our way, we do not care to know your courses.
What is Shaddai that we should worship him, and what good should we do when we invoked him?’
Here it is not in their hands that their comfort lies, wrong-doers’ principles are far from him—
How often do wrong-doers’ lamps go out and their calamity come upon them, cords grip them by his anger,
Do they become like straw before a wind and like chaff that a gale filches?
Let him not lay his misfortune away for his sons; let him pay it up to himself and let him know it.
Let his eyes see his calamity and let him drink ire of Shaddai.
For what concern has he for his family after him, when his number of months has been cut off?
—Should one teach the Deity knowledge, when it is he judges those on high?
This one dies in perfect soundness, all quiet and at ease,
His crocks are full of milk and the marrow of his bones has its drink,
And that one dies in bitter soul and has never eaten a comfortable meal;
Together they lie down on the clay and maggots cover them over.
Here, I know your ideas and such designs as you contemplate against me,
That you say ‘Where is an aristocrat’s house? and where are wrong-doers’ dwellings?’
Have you not asked travelers, and do you not recognize their tokens?
That the bad man is kept back on the day of calamity, gets the better of the day of wrath?
And who tells him of his course to his face? and if he has done a thing who pays him back?
And he is brought to burial and his mound is attended to.
Arroyo clods are sweet to him, and all men pour along after him and innumerable before him.
And how are you to comfort me with thin air, when your answers sift down to unreliability?”
And Eliphaz the Temanite answered
“Is a man to be serviceable to God? why, it is to himself that a capable man is serviceable.
Does Shaddai have any concern that you should do right, or any profit when you follow a conscientious course?
Would it be for your piety that he would reprove you and arraign you for judgment?
Is it not that your wickedness is great and your guilt infinite,
Because you demand pawns of your brothers without reason and strip off naked men’s garments,
Do not give a drink of water to a fainting man and refuse bread to a hungry man,
But a strong-handed man has the country for his own, and an influential man is to live in it;
You turn widows away empty-handed and batter orphans’ arms?
That is why there are traps around you and dread throws you into sudden consternation,
Light has turned dark for you, you cannot see, and spray of water covers you.
Of course, God stands high in the heavens and sees the heads of the stars, lofty though they be,
And you think ‘What does God know? will he judge through thick air?
Clouds are a screen to him and he will not see; and he will be walking the vault of the heavens.’
Will you keep to the foul-players’ path, the one villains have trodden,
Who were seized untimely, a river pouring upon their foundation,
Those who said to Deity ‘Get out of our way’ and ‘What should Shaddai do to us?’
When it was he that had filled their houses with good things; wrong-doers’ principles are far from him.
Honest men see and are glad, and an innocent man derides them:
‘They are positively annihilated, every mother’s son, and fire has consumed the last remnant of them.’
Get used to him and on good terms with him; by that what comes to you will be good.
Take an instruction from his mouth and lodge his say in your heart.
If you go back to Shaddai, humbling yourself, put foul play far off from your tent,
Lay ore in dust and Ophir gold among arroyo rocks,
Then Shaddai will be your nuggets and peak-silver to you.
For then you will be happy over Shaddai and raise your face to God,
You will invoke him and he will hear you and you will be paying your vows,
And you will decide on a thing and have it hold good for you, and light will be beaming over your paths.
For he brings low the lofty and proud man, and the man of downcast eyes he saves.
He will bring to safety one who is not innocent, and he shall be brought to safety by the cleanness of your hands.”
But Job answered
“Today too my complaint is rebellion! my hand lies heavy on my moans.
If only I knew how to find him, come to his seat!
I would formulate my case before him and fill my mouth with arguments;
I should find out what points he would make in answer to me, should see what he would say to me.
Would he maintain his contention against me by superior strength? not he, he would just pay attention to me.
There I should have one who was candid arguing with me, and I should definitively get clear from my judge.
Here I go east and he is not there, and west and I do not perceive him,
I look for him in the north and do not behold him, swing round to the south and do not see him,
While he knows which way I stand; were he to test me, I should come out like gold.
My foot holds on to his tracks, I watch his course and do not swerve,
From the command of his lips I do not shift, in my bosom I have laid up the say of his mouth.
But when he has his mind made up who will turn him back? he hankers and he acts.
For he will go through with what he has marked out for me, and has in store plenty of things like that.
That is why I am affrighted at him; I realize the situation and stand in dread of him,
And Deity has unnerved me and left me terror-struck.
For I do not break down at darkness and at being covered with blackness.
“How comes it times are not reserved by Shaddai and those who know him do not behold his days?
These displace boundary-marks, steal a flock and pasture it,
Drive off orphans’ donkeys, take a widow’s cow and hold it as a pawn,
Force needy men off the road; earth’s downtrodden go into hiding together.
They go out in the wilderness like wild asses in their activities in quest of anything that can be eaten; he has desert wastes as food for the boys.
On the range they make a harvest of its cattle-feed, they go through a wicked man’s vineyard for belated grapes.
They pass the night naked for want of clothing and coverless in the cold.
They are wet with mountain rainstorms and hug rocks for lack of shelter.
They steal orphan from breast and take in pawn a poverty-stricken man’s baby.
They go about naked for want of clothing, and while they go hungry they carry shocks of grain,
Between their walls they press oil, they tread winepresses and go thirsty.
Out of cities dying men groan and souls of men mortally wounded shriek. And God does not find any fault.
Those are rebels against light, do not recognize its routes nor settle in its paths.
When it is not light a murderer stands up, kills a downtrodden and needy man; and in the night a thief goes about.
And an adulterer’s eye watches for dusk, thinking ‘No eye will espy me,’ and he muffles up his face.
One breaks into houses in the dark. By day they shut themselves in; they make no acquaintance with light;
For alike are morning to them and gloom, because they are familiar with the wraiths of gloom.
He is light on the surface of water; their share in the land shall be cursed; a treader shall not turn to their vineyard.
Drought, heat too, steal snow-water; the realm of death, who have sinned.
The womb that fashioned him will forget him, his loftiness will not go on to be remembered, and foul play breaks like a piece of wood.
One who does injuries to a barren woman that bears no children, and no good to a widow,
And drags down needy men by his power, stands up and does not put faith in living;
He grants him to have confidence and reliance, and his eyes are on their courses.
They have been lofty a little while, and there is nothing of them and they are laid low, collapse like alkali-sorrel, and are cut down like heads of grain.
If not, then, who will show me up as a liar and reduce my claims to nothing?”
And Bildad the Shuhite answered
“Dominion and terror are about him; he makes peace in his realms aloft.
Is there any counting his regiments? and over whom does his light not stand up?
How is a human being to be in the right with Deity? and how is one born of woman to be pure?
Here the very moon is not bright and stars are not pure to his eyes,
To say nothing of a human being, a maggot; of a son of mankind, a worm!”
But Job answered
“What a help you have been to one without strength, what a salvation to an arm without energy,
What a counselor to one without wisdom, and in what abundance you have imparted common sense!
Whom have you told what to say? and whose breath came out from you?
The shades writhe underneath the water and its denizens.
The realm of death lies naked before him and the land of the gone forever has no cover.
He stretches the north over vacancy, hangs earth on nothing,
Bundles up water in his thunderclouds and the cloud does not tear under it,
Encloses the face of the full moon, spreading his cloud over it.
He has drawn a boundary circle on the face of the water at the extremity of light, where it meets darkness.
The pillars of the sky rock and are confounded at his rebuke.
By his power he stirred the sea and by his understanding he mangled Rahab.
By his wind the sky is swept bare, and his hand pierced the elusive snake.
There, these are the edges of his course, and what a whispered thing it is that we hear of him! but the thunder of his energies who may perceive?”
And Job further struck up his lay and said
“By the Deity, who has brushed aside my rights, and Shaddai, who has embittered my life,
When my breath was still all in me and God’s wind in my nostrils,
My lips shall not speak amiss nor my tongue voice false pretenses.
Away with the thought of my putting you in the right; till I breathe my last I will not throw off my conscientiousness.
I hold fast to my righteous cause and will not loosen my hold; my heart feels no remorse for any of my days.
May my enemy be in the state of a wrong-doer and my adversary in that of a knave!
For what is an ungodly man’s hope when God is cutting off and pulling out his soul?
Will Deity hear his cry when distress comes upon him,
Or will he be happy over Shaddai, call on God on every occasion?
I will instruct you as to the Deity’s hand; what Shaddai has in mind I will not conceal from you.
Here you have all of you seen the sights, what do you go into flights of fancy for?
This is a wicked man’s lot in the Deity’s plan, and the estate violent men are to get from Shaddai.
If his sons are numerous, the sword is for them, and his offspring will not have their fill of bread.
His survivors will be buried in death and his widows will not weep.
If he piles up silver like earth and lays up clothing as if it were clay,
He will lay it in and an honest man will wear it and innocent men share the silver among them.
He has built his house like a spider’s, like a booth a watchman makes.
He goes to bed rich, but is so no more; he opens his eyes and it is not there.
Dissolution descends upon him like water; in the night a gale snatches him,
An east wind picks him up and he goes, and it sweeps him out of his place.
He pelts him unsparingly; he is in constant flight from his hand.
He strikes his hands together over him and whistles at him from his place.
“For there is a mine for silver and a place for gold that they wash out.
Iron is taken out of earth, and one melts stone to copper.
Man has set an end to darkness, and to every extremity he ransacks stone of blackness and gloom.
An intruding people breaks into ravines that were forgotten by feet; they suffer privations, they rove from men
To a country from which bread has gone out and whose underpart turns to be like fire,
A place whose stones are malachite and which has clods of gold,
A path no bird of prey knows nor has a kite’s eye glimpsed it,
Which boldest beasts have not trodden nor lion passed along it.
He puts his hand to the pyrite rock, turns mountains up by their roots;
He rips out channels among the rocks, and his eye sees everything valuable.
He explores the sources of rivers and brings to light an undiscovered thing.
But where is wisdom to be had from, and what is the place for insight?
No man knows the road to it, and it is not to be found in the land of the living.
The deep says ‘it is not in me’ and the sea ‘I do not have it here.’
Solid gold is not to be given for it nor silver to be weighed out as its price;
It is not to be balanced against nuggets from Ophir, against the most precious beryl, or lapis lazuli;
Gold and glass will not match it, a thing of red gold be an exchange for it;
Pearls and alabaster are not to be mentioned, and wisdom is more of a prize than coral;
The Nubian chrysolite will not match it, nor against pure nugget-gold is it to be balanced;
And where does wisdom come from? and what is the place for insight?
It lies out of sight of any living thing and screened from the birds of the air.
Death and the land of the gone forever say ‘We have heard a hearsay of it.’
God understands the road to it, he knows the place for it,
Because he looks to the ends of the earth, sees under all the sky,
Determining a weight for the wind and proportioning the water by measure.
When he made a law of nature for the rain and a course for the lightning of thunder,
Then he saw it and described it, made it sure and thoroughly searched it out,
And he said to man ‘Here, fearing the Lord is wisdom and shunning what is bad is insight.’”
And Job further struck up his lay and said
“Would that I were as in old-time months, as in the days when God watched over me,
When he let his lamp beam over my head and by his light I walked through darkness!
As I was in my days of ripeness, when God had a fence round my home,
When Shaddai was still with me, my boys were around me,
When my callers washed their dust off in clabber and rocks on my grounds poured rills of oil.
When I went out of gate to town, prepared to take my seat in the square,
Young men saw me and hid and graybeards rose and stood;
Captains checked what they had to say and laid hand on their mouths;
Magistrates’ voices hid and their tongues stuck to the roof of their mouths.
For ears heard and deemed me happy, eyes saw and bore witness to me,
That I brought a downtrodden suppliant out of trouble, and an orphan, and one whom none would help;
The blessing of one who was perishing came upon me and I set a widow’s heart caroling.
I clothed myself in right, and like a robe and tiara justice clothed me.
I was eyes for the blind man, and feet for the lame man was I.
I was a father to the needy, and investigated the claims of the man I did not know
And smashed a knave’s fangs and knocked prey out of his teeth.
And I thought I should breathe my last with my nestlings and have my days as numerous as the sand,
With my roots spreading out to water and dew on my twigs through the night,
My honors fresh about me and my bow coming new in my hand.
They listened for me and waited, kept still to get my advice;
After my word they did not speak again, and my discourse came sprinkling down on them.
They waited for me as if for rain and held their mouths wide open for a spring shower.
I gave them a laugh, they did not believe; and my face shone, they did not let theirs fall.
I chose their course and sat as head, and lived like a king in a raiding-party, as if he were comforting mourners.
But now my juniors are laughing at me, whose fathers I had rejected for placing with my sheep-dogs.
Of what use was even the strength of their hands to me, men in whom solid vigor was lost, gaunt with destitution and starvation?
Those who gnaw arid downs, the emesh of blast and blight,
Who pluck alkali-sorrel, wormwood leaves, and have broom-roots for their bread;
They are driven out of a community, they yell at them as they would at a thief.
They have to live in the sides of arroyos, in holes in the ground and between stones.
They bray between wormwood bushes, snuggle together under weeds.
Sons of rascals, sons of nobody that can be named, they are whipped out of the country.
—And now I am the butt of their jingles and have become a byword of theirs.
They abhor me, stand far away from me, do not keep their spit out of my face.
For he has undone my bowstring and made me helpless, and they loosen their reins before me.
On the right a horde stand up, unsettle my footing, and build their tracks of calamity against me.
They tear up my path, do great work for catastrophe, have nobody to help them.
They come like coming through a broad breach, roll along under the crash of ruin.
Dissolution turns upon me, my dignity is chased off as if by the wind, and my hope of succor passes like a cloud.
And now I have my life draining out, days of suffering are gripping me,
In the night my bones are being dug away and my sinews get no repose.
My garment takes strong hold, lies snug on me like the neck of my shirt.
He has laid me for clay, and I am made like earth and ashes.
I clamor to you and you do not answer me; I stand there and you observe me,
You turn brutal toward me, you wreak your grudge on me with the vast strength of your hand.
You pick me up into the air, ride me on the wind, let storm toss me.
For I know you will bring me back to death, to the rendezvous of everything alive.
Only he does not lay hands on a heap of ruin; or by his disaster will there be lucre for them?
I did weep for the man who was having a hard time, my soul grieved for the needy man;
I hoped for good, and evil came; I awaited light, and murky darkness came.
My vitals are boiling, never still; days of suffering confront me.
I go in mourning without sunshine, stand up and clamor publicly.
I am brother to jackals and fellow to ostriches.
My skin blackens and comes off, and my bones are hot with fever.
And my lyre has turned to mourning and my pipe to the voices of weepers.
“I put my eyes under a contract, and how was I to take notice of a maiden?
And what is God’s allotment from above and Shaddai’s assignment from on high?
Is it not calamity for a knave and mishap for villains?
Does not he see my courses and count all my steps?
If I walked with false pretense and my foot hurried toward fraud,
Let God weigh me in a fair balance and know about my conscientiousness.
If my tread has swerved from the course and my eye has followed my heart and anything has stuck to my hands,
Let me sow and another eat, and what grows for me be uprooted.
If my heart has been inveigled after a woman and I have lain in wait at my friend’s doorway,
Let my wife grind for another and others crouch over her.
For that would be lewdness, it would be guilt to come before a court.
For that is a fire that would eat down to the land of the gone forever and take out the roots of all my produce.
If I refused the rights of my slaves when they had a dispute with me,
What should I do when Deity stands up, and when he is punishing what answer should I make to him?
Did not he who made me in a mother’s body make them, and was it not one who worked us into shape in the womb?
If I withheld what poor men wanted and let a widow’s eyes wear out with looking and longing,
And ate my snack alone and an orphan did not eat part
(For from my boyhood I raised him as a father would, and ever since my birth I helped her along),
If I saw one perishing for lack of clothing and that a needy man had nothing to cover him,
If his back did not bless me and he get warmth out of the fleeces of my sheep,
If I shook my fist at a quiet man because I saw I had friends in court,
May my arm drop off from its shoulder, may it be broken through its long bone.
For Deity’s calamity is a thing I dread, and I cannot cope with his majesty.
If I have made gold my reliance and spoken of kethem as my confidence,
If I was gladdened because my wealth was great and I had a great deal at my disposal,
If I saw the light as it beamed and the moon walking sublimely
And I was secretly so simpleminded that my mouth kissed my hand,
That too would be guilt to come before a court, for I should have been lying to Deity above.
If I was glad of a disaster to one who hated me and was elated because evil had found him—
Why, I did not let my throat sin asking his life with a curse;
If the men of my tent did not say ‘Who will bring somebody that has not had all he wanted of his meat?’—
No visitor from abroad spent the night in the street; I opened my doors to the wayfarer.
If in human fashion I covered up my crime, burying my guilt under my cloak,
Because I stood in awe of a great crowd and the contempt of clans dismayed me, And I kept quiet, not going out of the doorway—
I wish I had someone to hear me! Here is my signature, let Shaddai answer me! And a bill that my opponent had written,
wouldn’t I carry it on my shoulder, lace it on as a crown for me!
I would report to him the number of my steps, would receive him as a lord high steward should.
If my soil cries out against me and its furrows are weeping together,
If I have eaten its strength without paying money and have let the life go out of its owners,
Instead of wheat let briers come out, and instead of barley nightshade.” End of the words of Job.
And these three men left off answering Job, because he felt that he was in the right.
And Elihu the son of Barakel the Buzite, of the clan of Ram, was angry: angry at Job for making himself out in the right against God,
and angry at his three friends for not finding an answer, and putting God in the wrong.
And Elihu had waited for Job in the talk because they were older than he,
but Elihu saw that the three men had no answer in their mouths, and was angry.
And Elihu the son of Barakel the Buzite answered “I am a youngster and you are gray-bearded men; that was why I was bashful and afraid to state my view among you.
I thought ‘Let days speak and number of years disclose wisdom.’
But it is a spirit in man, after all, and Shaddai’s breath makes them understand things.
It is not men of many days that are wise nor old men that understand what is right.
So I say, Hear me; I too will state my view.
Here I did wait for your words, listened for your discernments, Till you should hunt out something to say,
and applied my attention to you, And found Job had nobody to confute him, to answer his say, among you.
For fear you should say ‘We have discovered wisdom,’ Deity shall put him to rout, not a man.
And he has not marshaled points against me, nor will I answer him with what you said.
“They were dismayed, no longer made any answer, their phrases had moved out,
And was I to wait when they were not speaking, when they were at a standstill, no longer made any answer?
I will make the answer that is my portion, I too will state my view,
For I am full of things to be said, the spirit in my waist is putting me under a strain,
I feel my waist like wine that is not being opened; as with skins of new wine, an explosion is coming.
I will speak and get relief, will open my lips and answer.
May I not show partiality to any man; and to no human being will I pay compliments,
For I do not know how to pay compliments; my Maker might easily snatch me away.
But hear what I have to say, Job, and give ear to all my words.
Here I am opening my mouth, my tongue is speaking under its roof,
My say is the sincere expression of my heart and my lips utter the best of their knowledge.
Deity’s spirit made me and Shaddai’s breath put life into me.
Answer me if you can, join issue and stand up to me.
You will find me to be in the same relation to Deity as you; I was kneaded out of clay as you were.
Here will terror of me not overwhelm you nor my duress weigh you down.
“Only—you said in my hearing, I heard a sound of such words,
‘I am pure, free from crime, I am clear and have no guilt about me.
Here he is inventing antagonisms against me and counting me as an enemy of his,
Setting my feet in the stocks and watching all my paths.’
Here you are not right in this, I answer you, because God is more than man.
How come you setting up a case against him because he does not answer all your words?
For Deity speaks once for all and does not repeat it a second time.
In a dream, a vision of the night, when trances fall on men, in slumbers on the bed,
Then he makes disclosure to men and dismays them with sights that they see,
To turn away man from his doings and prune away pride from a man,
Hold back his life from the grave and his being from rushing upon destruction.
And he is admonished by pain on the bed and the discord in his bones is perpetual,
And his inclination loathes bread and his appetite the food it naturally craves.
His flesh gets too wasted to look at and his bones so bare nobody will look at them,
And his life is near to the grave and his being to the place of the dead.
If he has over him an angel, an interpreter, one out of a thousand, to tell man his right course,
And he is gracious to him and says ‘Let him off from going down to the Pit; I have been given satisfaction,’
His flesh will grow plumper than in childhood; he will come back to his youth.
He will invoke God and God will accept him, and he will see his face with shouts of joy; and he will give the man back his standing for righteousness.
He will sing before men and say ‘I sinned, I turned fair play to foul, and he did not give ma measure for measure,
He has redeemed my life from passing into the Pit, and my being has the sight of the light.’
Here Deity does all these things twice over, three times, with a man,
To turn his life back from the Pit to be lighted with the light of life;
Listen, Job, hear me, be silent for me to speak.
If there is anything to be said, answer me; speak, because I should like you to be in the right.
If there is not, hear me yourself; be silent and let me acquaint you with wisdom.”
And Elihu answered
“Wise men, hear my words; give ear to me, men of knowledge;
For ears test words and a palate tastes food.
Let us pick out rights and come to an understanding of what is good,
Because Job says ‘I am virtuous but Deity has taken away my rights;
Against my rights I am to be lying and I have a festering arrow in me without a crime.’
Who is such a man as Job, who drinks scurrility like water
And takes the route to fellowship with villains and to company with criminals?
Because he says ‘It is of no advantage to a man to be on good terms with God.’
So, men of sense, hear me: away with the thought of wrong-doing on Deity’s part, foul play on Shaddai’s,
For he will pay man back appropriately to what he does, and give each one the experiences proper to the path he takes.
In real truth Deity does not do wrong nor Shaddai play tricks with justice.
Who put him in charge of earth? and who established the whole universe?
If he should draw his spirit back to himself and take up to himself his breath,
All creatures of flesh would expire together and man would go back to clay.
And if you are in your senses, listen to me; give ear to the point I make.
Is it even to be that one who hates justice holds sway or a great right-doer does wrong?
He who says ‘reprobate’ to a king and ‘iniquitous’ to noblemen,
Who does not defer to generals nor recognize a prominent man before a poor man, because they are all the work of his hands?
They die in a moment, at midnight; he touches prominent men and they pass by, and removes a formidable fighter without turning a hand.
For his eyes are on a man’s courses and he sees all his steps;
There is no darkness, no gloom, that villains may be veiled in.
For a man does not have a date set him to go to Deity for a trial;
He breaks great men without an investigation and sets up others in their place.
So he is aware of their works, and overthrows in the night and they are beaten down.
For wrong-doers he cuffs them in a place with spectators,
Seeing that they had turned off from following him and not been regardful of any of his courses,
Bringing in before him a poor man’s outcry and letting him hear the outcry of downtrodden men.
But if he is quiet who is to condemn? or if he veils his face who is to behold him? be it over a nation or over a man alike,
That an ungodly man may not be king, a people’s trap.
For does he say to Deity ‘I bear; I will not do harmful things;
What I do not see, teach me yourself; if I have done amiss I will not keep on’?
Was he to make requital on the basis of your ideas, that you are vetoing? For you are to choose, not I; what you know, speak out!
Men of brains will say to me, and a wise man who hears me,
Job speaks not by knowledge and his words do not run by common sense.
Let Job be kept under test permanently for answers that put him among villains!
For he adds rebelliousness to his sin, slaps his hands between us and talks volubly to the Deity.”
And Elihu answered
“Do you think this right, say ‘my good case before Deity,’
That you ask how it benefits you, ‘What good do I get more than by my sinning?’
I give you the answer, and your comrades with you,
Look at the sky and see, and behold the ether so high above you;
If you have sinned what are you doing to him, and if your crimes are many what effect has it on him?
If you have done right what are you giving to him, or what is he getting at your hands?
Your wrong-doing pertains to a man like yourself and your right-doing to a human being.
They cry out over the great number of denials of justice, they clamor over powerful men’s high hand,—
And one has not said ‘Where is God my Maker, who gives songs in the night,
Who teaches us more than the beasts of earth and makes us wiser than the birds of the air?’
It is there that they cry unanswered because of the pride of bad men,
All in vain—Deity does not hear and Shaddai does not regard it.
Even when you say you do not behold him, he has the case before him and you are to wait for him.
And now because he does not set his anger to work he does not thoroughly know the offense!
But Job is opening his mouth to let out air, uttering big phrases without knowing what he is talking about.”
And Elihu said further
“Wait a bit and I will show you, for there is more to say for God.
I will take a broad view and credit my Maker with doing right.
What I have to say is no falsification; you have with you one who is sincere in his views.
Lo, Deity is supreme and will not be disdainful, supreme in power of mind.
He will not let a wrong-doer live and will give downtrodden men their rights.
He will not minimize his attention to a right-doer, but with kings will enthrone them permanently, and they shall be exalted.
And if they are bound in fetters, caught in cords of misery,
He tells them of their doings and their offenses, that they were overweening,
And makes disciplinary disclosures to them and says they are to turn back from vileness.
If they listen and submit they shall finish their days in good living and their years in comfort;
But if they do not listen they will rush upon destruction and come to their end by lack of knowledge.
But men of godless heart take to anger, do not cry out petitions when he binds them;
Their vital spark shall die off in youth and their lives as do sodomite boys.
He rescues an unfortunate man in his misfortune and makes disclosures to them in privations.
And he has been enticing you out of the mouth of distress too, unconstrained roominess under it, and the setting down of your table full of rich food.
And you are full of the sentence on a wrong-doer; judgment and sentence take hold,
For let not choler entice you into mockery nor abundance of composition-money deflect you.
Will your clamor take effect without distress, and all exertions of strength?
Do not pant for the night, to have peoples go up where they stand.
Beware, do not turn to depravity, for you have been preferring this to suffering.
Lo, Deity shows himself supernal in his strength; who is such a preceptor as he?
Who has appointed his course for him, and who has said ‘You have done amiss’?
Remember to extol his work, of which men have sung.
All mankind view it, man looks at it from afar.
Lo, Deity is great beyond our knowledge; the number of his years is incalculable.
For he takes away drops from the sea to filter as rain for his mist,
Which the heavens let trickle down and let drop upon many a man.
Or does one understand the spreading of clouds either? the resoundings of his bower?
Lo, he spreads his mist about him and covers mountaintops.
For by them he provisions peoples, gives food on a great scale.
He covers a stone with light and orders it to strike a mark,
Assailing mischief and wrong and wreaking jealous anger on foul play.
My heart is alarmed too at this and jumps out of its place.
Hear, hear the commotions of his voice and what comes as a mutter from his mouth!
He sends it abroad under all the sky and his light over the edges of the earth.
Behind it a voice roars; he thunders with his sublime voice and does not hold them back when his voice is heard;
Deity thunders with his voice wondrously. He does things great beyond our knowledge,
For he says to the snow ‘Fall to earth’ and showers down his mighty rains.
He seals up every human being’s hands that all men may know his work;
And beasts go into coverts and lodge in their dens.
Out of the Chamber comes a gale and out of Mezarim cold weather.
By Deity’s breath ice is put in and the breadth of water is in curbs.
Also he loads a cloud with refreshment, cloudy sky scatters his fall rain,
And it goes circling about by his guidance that they may do all that he orders them to over the world on the ground,
If for a cudgel, if for his earth, if for kindness he sends it to its goal.
Give ear to this, Job; stand still and realize Deity’s wonders.
Do you know how God lays their charge on them and the light of his clouds beams out?
Do you know about the hovering of clouds, the wonders of him who is faultless in skill?
Will you whose clothes grow hot when earth has quietness from the south
Be with him to consolidate heavens strong as a metal mirror?
Let us know what to say to him; we cannot get it in order for darkness.
Is he to be told the story of my speaking? or does any man think of being swept away?
And now they do not see light, it is a bright spot in the heavens; but a wind goes over and clears them.
From the north comes resplendence; over God there is a refulgence that is terrible.
Shaddai—our minds do not reach to him, ample in strength and justice and great in right-dealing; he will not victimize.
So men fear him; he does not take notice of any wise-headed men.”
But Jehovah answered Job out of the tempest
“Who is this that is befogging a discussion by phrases without knowledge?
Gird your loins like a man so that I may ask you questions and you inform me.
Where were you when I laid the foundation of earth? tell, if you have competent knowledge.
Who determined its dimensions? for you know! or who stretched a measuring-line over it?
On what were its under-foundations planted? or who laid its cornerstone
While the morning stars shouted together and all the angels hurrahed?
Who enclosed the sea with doors when it came bursting out of the womb,
When I made clouds its clothing and thick air its wrapping
And broke a boundary for it and set a bar and doors,
And said ‘You are to come to here but not beyond, and here the pride of your waves shall break’?
Did you ever in your life command a morning, let a dawn know its place
To take hold of earth’s edges that wrong-doers may be shaken out of it?
It takes shape like clay printed with a stamp, and colors like a dress,
And wrong-doers have their light withheld, and a high-raised arm is broken.
Have you come to the sources of the sea and gone inspecting through the deep?
Have the gates of death been laid open for you, or the gatemen of gloom been afraid at sight of you?
Have you applied your attention to the breadths of earth? tell, if you know it all.
In which direction does light have its home, and which is the place for darkness?
Because you get it at its domain and are expert in the paths to its house.
You know, because you were born then and the number of your days is great!
Have you been into the reserves of snow, and seen the reserves of hail
Which I am holding back for a day of crisis, a day of battle and war?
In which direction is wind divided, east wind scattered over earth?
Who laid out a system of channels for floods and a course for the lightning of thunder,
To send rain on a country without a man, a wilderness with no human being in it,
To satisfy the hunger of blasted and blighted places and to make a thirsty place grow vegetation?
Does the rain have a father? or who brought dewdrops to birth?
Out of whose body did the ice come? and who gave birth to hoarfrost?
Water masks itself like a stone and the surface of the deep coheres.
Shall you be tying the laces of the Pleiades or unhitching the traces of Orion,
Making Mazzaroth come out at its time and guiding Aldebaran with its sons under it?
Do you know the laws of the sky or are you ordaining its supervision of the earth?
Will you send your voice aloft to the cloud and have a spray of water cover you?
Will you send lightnings abroad, and have them go and say to you ‘Here we are’?
Who implanted wisdom in the ibis? or who gave discernment to the cock?
Who counts in wisdom the threads of mare’s-tail clouds, and the water-bags of the sky who tips down
When loam runs into metal and clods cling together?
Will you hunt prey for a lioness and fill the need of two-year-old lions
When they are down in the lairs, sitting in ambush in a covert?
Who gets its provision ready for the raven when its young are clamoring to Deity, wandering about in want of food?
Do you know crag ibexes’ birth, watch does’ calving?
Do you count the months they fill out, and know their birth-date?
They crouch down, detach their young, let go what they have been hampered with;
Their children are robust, grow big in the wilds, go out and never come back.
Who set free a wild ass and unhitched an onager’s halter,
Of which I have made desert the home, alkali plains the habitation?
It laughs at town noises, hears no vociferations of a driver.
It explores mountains as its pasture and searches after any green thing.
Will a ure be willing to work for you or come to your crib for the night?
Will you tie a yoke on him with cords or will he harrow vales after you?
Will you put confidence in him because his strength is great, and leave to him the results of your toil?
Will you rely on him to come back, get in your seed to your threshing-floor?
An ostrich’s wing is for pleasure; or is it a kindly pinion and plume,
When she leaves her eggs on the ground and warms them on the earth,
And has forgotten that feet will smash them and wild animals tread them to pieces?
She is hardhearted to her young as if they were not hers; her labor goes for nothing without alarming her,
Because God has made her unmindful of wisdom and given her no allowance of sense.
The minute she goes off high she laughs at the pony and its rider.
Do you give the ponies mettle? do you clothe their necks with mane?
Do you set them in commotion like grasshoppers? the thrill of their snorting is a terror.
They paw in the vale and are joyous, go out in strength to meet an armament,
Laugh at terrors and are not dismayed, and do not turn back before swords.
On them ring quiver, spearhead, and javelin.
Twitching and fidgeting they pit the earth and do not believe there is a sound of a ram-horn.
At every ram-horn they say ‘Ha!’ and scent battle afar, thunder of captains and cheering.
Is it by your sagacity a hawk takes wing, soars off to the south,
Or is it by your direction that a vulture goes high and that it sets its nest aloft,
Perches on a crag and spends the night on a crag-tooth and a fastness,
Searches from there for food, its eyes looking far away,
And feeds its chicks with blood, and where there are corpses, there the bird is?”
And Jehovah answered Job
“Does an admonisher dispute with Shaddai? let him who corrects God answer it.”
And Job answered Jehovah
“Here I am, insignificant—what reply should I make? I lay my hand on my mouth.
I did speak once, but will not answer— and twice; but I will do it no more.”
And Jehovah answered Job out of a tempest
“Gird your loins like a man so that I may ask you questions and you inform me.
Will you even quash my judgment, hold me in the wrong so that you may be in the right?
Or do you have an arm like God’s, do you thunder with a voice like his?
Bedeck yourself with dignity and sublimity, robing yourself in majesty and splendor,
Hurl the rages of your anger, and see every proud one and bring him low,
See every overweening one and humble him, crumple wrong-doers where they stand,
Bury them in the ground together, envelop their faces in sod,
And I too will praise you that your right hand has made good your cause.
Here is Behemoth, that I made with you; it eats grass like cattle.
Here is the strength in its back and the vigor in the muscles of its belly.
It holds its tail stiff as a cedar; the sinews of its hams are ropy.
Its bones are copper pipes, its backbone like a bar of iron.
First of Deity’s undertakings is this, made as he was bringing on his chisel.
For mountains bear growth for it, and all beasts of the wilds play there.
Under jujube-trees it lies, in a blind of reeds and morass,
Jujube-trees cover it with its shade, arroyo poplars surround it.
Suppose a river overflows, it is not nervous; it is undaunted though a Jordan bursts against its mouth;
In its eyes it takes it; it has its nose bored with baits.
Will you pull Leviathan about with a fishhook and press its tongue down with a line?
Will you run a rush through its nose and punch its gills with a thorn?
Will it give you profuse appeals for grace, or speak submissively to you?
Will it make terms with you and you take it as permanent slave?
Will you play with it as you would with a bird and tie it up for your girls,
Cooperators bargain over it, divide it between dealers?
Will you fill its skin with darts, its head with fish-harpoons?
Lay your hand on it, think of fighting— do not try it again.
Here his expectation has been belied, at the very sight of it he is sent flying,
He is not fierce enough to rouse it— and who will stand his ground before me?
Who has confronted me and come off safe and sound? under all the sky mine he is.
I will not be silent as to its members, and the matter of powerfulness, and the symmetry of its build.
Who uncovers the surface of its coat? who will get inside its double coat of mail?
Who opens the doors of its mouth? the circuit of its teeth is a terror.
Its back is ridged with shields, closed in tight sealing,
One coming up to another with no gap intervening,
Each keeping contact with the next, inseparably linked.
Its sneezing sends beams of light and its eyes are like the eyelashes of the dawn;
Out of its mouth fly torches, sparks of fire escape;
Out of its nostrils smoke streams out like that from a heated pot and rushes.
Its breath sets coals ablaze, and a flame comes out of its mouth.
Force lodges on its neck and despair bounds before it.
The underparts of its flesh cling fast, are immovably welded on.
Its heart is solid as a stone and solid as a lower millstone.
At its rearing up heroes quail, at bone-breaking strokes they fall into dismay.
One who hits it with a sword finds that that does not bite, a spear nor a bolt nor a mail-piercer.
It thinks iron is threshed straw and bronze rotten wood.
A shaft from a bow will not put it to flight; stones from a sling turn to straw for it.
A club counts as a straw for it, and it laughs at the vibration of a javelin.
Under it are sharp chips of crockery; it runs a toothed plank over mud.
It makes ooze boil up like a pot, makes sea like a perfumer’s saucepan.
It leaves a shining wake behind it; one thinks the deep is gray-haired.
Over the earth there is nothing that masters it, it that is made to be without dismay.
Every high one fears it; it is king over all proud beasts.?
And Job answered Jehovah
“I know that you can do everything and nothing you may think of is impossible to you.
Who is this that is muddling a discussion without knowing anything about it? so I have been asserting things I do not understand, things too mysterious for me, which I do not know:
‘Listen, and I will speak; I will put questions; inform me.’
I had heard of you by hearsay, but now my eye has seen you;
Therefore I recant and repent in the ashes on the ground.”
And after Jehovah had spoken these words to Job, Jehovah said to Eliphaz the Temanite “I am angry with you and your two friends because you did not speak soundly about me as my servant Job did.

Now take seven steers and seven rams and go to my servant Job and offer them as burnt-offering for yourselves and let my servant Job pray for you, and see if I will do him the personal favor of not ill-treating you because you did not speak soundly of me as my servant Job did.”
And Eliphaz the Temanite and Bildad the Shuhite and Sophar the Naʽamathite went and did as Jehovah had told them to, and Jehovah did do the favor for Job.
And Jehovah came back to Job when he prayed for his friends; and Jehovah added double to everything that belonged to him.

And all his brothers and sisters and all his former acquaintances came to him and ate bread with him in his house and lamented over him and comforted him for all the disaster Jehovah had brought upon him, and gave him a keshitah each and a gold earring each.
And Jehovah blessed Job’s later life more than his earlier, and he had fourteen thousand sheep and goats and six thousand camels and a thousand yoke of cattle and a thousand donkeys;
and he had seven sons and three daughters,
and named one daughter Jemimah and the second Kesi’ah and the third Keren-hap-Puk;
and there were no women so beautiful as Job’s daughters to be found in all the country; and their father gave them an inheritance among their brothers.
And Job lived after this a hundred and forty years, and saw his sons and his sons’ sons to four generations.
And Job died an old man, having lived as long as he cared to.
Happy the man who has not gone by wrong-doers’ policy nor stood in sinners’ road nor sat in cynics’ session,
But finds pleasure in Jehovah’s instructions, and his instructions he studies day and night.
And he will be like a tree planted by channels of water that bears its fruit in season, and its leaves never fade, and in all he does he will succeed.
Not so wrong-doers; not so, but like chaff that a wind blows about.
Therefore wrong-doers will not stand in judgment nor sinners in a congregation of honest men,
For Jehovah knows honest men’s courses, but wrong-doers’ courses will be lost.
Why have nations forgathered and peoples made empty propositions?
Kings of earth took their stand and potentates concerted a program against Jehovah and against his Anointed,
“Let us snap their tether and tear off their ropes.”
He who sits in heaven will laugh; the Lord will deride them.
Then he will speak to them in his anger and throw them into consternation by his heat,
“But I, I have invested my king on my sacred mountain Sion.”
I will tell the story of Jehovah’s ordinance: He said to me “You are my son, I myself have today given you birth.
Ask me and I will make nations your estate and the ends of earth your holding.
You shall break them with iron truncheon, smash them like crockery.”
And now, kings, be canny; take your lesson to heart, judges of earth;
Worship Jehovah in fear and kiss his feet with quaking,
For fear he should be angry and you perish right away, because his anger takes fire easily. Happy are all that take refuge in him.
(A psalm of David’s when he was in flight before his son Absalom.)
Jehovah, how thick come my foes! Many are standing up against me,
Many are saying of my soul “There is no help for him in his God.” (Selah)
But you, Jehovah, are a shield before me, my glory and the uplifter of my head.
Aloud to Jehovah I call, and he has answered me from his sacred mountain. (Selah)
I have lain down and gone to sleep and waked up, because Jehovah supports me.
I will not be afraid of thousands upon thousands of people who on all sides have beset me.
Stand up, Jehovah, save me, my God; For you have struck all my enemies on the jaw, broken the teeth of malefactors.
Salvation is a thing of Jehovah’s; your blessing be on your people! [Selah]
(Of the Director; with string accompaniment. A psalm of David’s.)
When I call answer me, my God of the righteous cause: in distress you have relieved me; be gracious to me and hear my prayer.
Gentlemen, how long—heavy-witted ones, what for— will you love emptiness, seek after a lie? (Selah)
But know that Jehovah has distinguished a man of his friendship; Jehovah will hear when I call to him.
Tremble and do not sin; tell yourselves as you lie in your beds, and be quiet. (Selah)
Offer rightful sacrifices and trust to Jehovah.
Many are saying “Who will let us see anything good?” Lift up over us the light of your face, Jehovah.
You have put gladness in our hearts surpassing the time their grain and grape-juice are plentiful.
In peace I will lie down and go right to sleep, because you solely, Jehovah, cause me to live in security.
(Of the Director; to the woodwind. A psalm of David’s.)
Give ear to my say, Jehovah! take in my moan!
Listen to the sound of my clamor, my King and God, for it is to you I pray.
Jehovah, in the morning you shall hear my voice, in the morning I will address you and be on the lookout.
For you are not a crime-loving deity, wickedness will not make its home with you,
Wild men will not take their stand under your eyes, you hate all that commit villainy,
You will destroy those who speak lies; Jehovah detests a man of bloodshed and fraud.
But I by the abundance of your friendship will enter your house, will do reverence toward your holy temple in your fear.
Jehovah, guide me in your righteousness on account of my ill-wishers, lay your way out straight before me.
For there is nothing solid in their mouths; their inward thought is catastrophe; their throats are open graves; they keep their tongues slippery.
Hold them to the penalty, God; let them come to a fall by their plans; for the multiplicity of their crimes banish them, because they have disobeyed you;
And let all that take refuge in you be glad And carol forever, you sheltering them, and let those who love your name exult in you,
Because you, Jehovah, bless an honest man, envelop him with goodwill like a shield.
(Of the Director; with string accompaniment; bass voices. A psalm of David’s.)
Jehovah, do not correct me in your anger nor chastise me in your ire;
Do me a kindness, Jehovah, because I am forlorn; make me well, Jehovah, because my bones are flinching.
My soul is flinching utterly; Jehovah, how long will you?
Come back, Jehovah, rescue my soul; save me for your friendship’s sake.
For in death there is no remembrance of you, in the world below who will give you thanks?
I am tired with moaning; all night I wash my bed with my tears; I melt down my bedstead.
My eyes have been wearing away for vexation, aging by all that distress me.
Away from me, all you that commit villainy, for Jehovah has heard the sound of my weeping,
Jehovah has heard my petition, Jehovah will receive my prayer.
All my enemies will be in great shame and consternation, will turn back and be in sudden shame.
(A dithyramb of David’s which he sang to Jehovah about the affair of Cush a Benjamite.)
Jehovah, my God, in you I take refuge: save me from all my persecutors and deliver me,
For fear he should make prey of my life like a lion, bringing down, and nobody rescuing.
Jehovah, my God, if I did this, if there is foul play in my hands,
If I injured one who was at peace with me and wantonly harassed one who was my foe,
Let an enemy chase after my soul and run it down and trample my life to the earth, and my glory be lodged in the dust. (Selah)
Rise in your anger, Jehovah; up with you against my foemen’s wrath, and bestir yourself to reach me. A judgment you have ordained;
let a congregation of gods surround you, and above them sit aloft.
Jehovah is arbiter of peoples: give judgment for me, Jehovah, in accordance with my fair dealing and the integrity I cherish;
Let wrong-doers’ evil disappear and right-doing be made regular— the Tester of Heads and Hearts is a right-doing God!
My shield is carried by God, saver of men of upright heart.
God is an honest man’s judge and the Deity is hostile to schemers.
If he does not turn back, he sharpens his sword, has strung his bow and bent it,
And got ready instruments of death, makes his arrows fireballs.
Here he is in labor with villainy, has become pregnant with mischief and will give birth to lies.
He has dug and sunk a pitfall and tumbled into the trap he was making.
His mischief will come back on his own head and his outrage come down on his own pate.
I thank Jehovah as befits his right-doing and sing a psalm to the name of Jehovah Most High.
(Of the Director; to the Gittith. A psalm of David’s.)
Jehovah, our Lord, how grand is your name throughout the earth, you whose majesty reaches above the sky,
Who out of the mouths of children at play and babies at the breast have laid a foundation of might on account of those who are foes to you, to put a stop to enemy and avenger!
When I see your sky, the work of your fingers, moon and stars that you have set,
What is man that you should remember him, any of humankind that you should attend to him?
And you have made him little short of God, with state and glory you crown him,
And have given him rule over the works of your hands, have placed everything under his feet,
Sheep and cattle all, beasts of the wilds too;
Bird of air and fish of sea, those that traverse fluid paths.
Jehovah our Lord, how grand is your name throughout the earth!
(Of the Director; falsetto voices. Of Ben’s. A psalm of David’s.)
I will give thanks to Jehovah with all my heart; I will tell the story of all your wonders;
I will be glad and exult in you, I will sing psalms to your name, Most High,
For my enemies’ turning to go backward, stumbling and perishing before you;
For you have given me justice and my rights, you sit enthroned as a fair judge.
You rebuke nations, you destroy a wrong-doer, you blot out their name forever and evermore.
The enemy are all gone, perpetual wastes, and cities you have uprooted; their memory has perished,
But Jehovah will stand fast forever, he has planted his throne for judgment,
And he will judge the world honestly, give fair verdicts for many a folk,
So that Jehovah may be a fastness for the downtrodden man, a fastness for hard times,
And those who know your name may have confidence in you, because you have never abandoned those who resort to you.
Sing psalms to Jehovah, him who is seated on Sion; tell among the peoples his deeds;
For a prosecutor of bloodshed remembers them; he never forgets the crying of unhappy men.
Be gracious to me, Jehovah; see my unhappy state because of those who hate me, you who uplift me from the gates of death,
So that I may tell all the story of your praises, exult in your salvation at the gates of the daughter of Sion.
Nations have sunk in a pitfall they had made; in a net that they hid their own feet are caught.
Jehovah has won recognition, has done justice; a wrong-doer is snared in the work of his own hands. (Higgaion. Selah)
Wrong-doers shall go back to the world below; all nations are forgetful of God.
For a needy man will not be perpetually forgotten, humble men’s hopes will not be lost forevermore.
Up, Jehovah; let man not be high and mighty; let nations bring their causes before you for judgment.
Put them in fear, Jehovah; let nations know they are human beings. (Selah)
Why do you stand aloof, Jehovah, ignore hard times?
Pridefully a wrong-doer chases a poor wretch— they shall be caught in the designs they have thought up.
For a wrong-doer praises, a grasping man blesses, on the basis of his own heart’s desire.
A wrong-doer loftily insults Jehovah, does not look out for his anger; All his calculations are that there is no God.
His courses are persistent at every time; Your judgments are too exalted to come within his view; all his foemen he pooh-poohs.
He says to himself “I shall be unshaken, for generation upon generation I shall be firm, to disaster I shall never succumb.”
His mouth is full of fraud and extortion; under his tongue are mischief and villainy.
He sits in village ambushes, kills innocent men under cover. His eyes are in wait for a wretched man.
He lies in wait under cover like a lion in its thicket, Lies in wait to catch a poor fellow, catches a poor fellow by drawing his net:
He beats down, brings low; wretches have fallen by his force.
He says to himself “Deity has forgotten, has veiled his face, does not see forevermore.”
Up, Jehovah! Deity, lift your hand! do not forget miserable men!
On what ground has a wrong-doer been contemptuous of God, said to himself you would not look into it?
You do see, because you look at mischief and offense, to put it into your hands; To you the orphan wretch leaves his cause; you have been a helper.
Break the arm of a wrong-doer and rascal; you look for his criminal work, it is not to be found.
Jehovah is king of ages on ages, heathen nations perish out of his country.
Humble men’s desire you have heard, Jehovah, the address of their hearts;
You sharpen your ear to judge orphan and downtrodden; Never again let a man out of the earth be arrogant.
(Of the Director. Of David’s.)
In Jehovah I take refuge: how is it you say to my soul “Flit mountainward like a sparrow”?
For here have the wicked strung their bow, Set their arrow on the string, in gloom to shoot at right-minded men.
When the foundations are torn up what does an honest man do?
Jehovah is in his holy temple; Jehovah has his throne in the sky; His eyes view, his glances test, the sons of men.
Jehovah tests honest man and rascal, and his nature hates a lover of outrage.
He will rain on rascals burning charcoal and sulfur, and scorching wind is the cup poured out for them.
For Jehovah is honest, loves honest doings; upright men shall behold his face.
(Of the Director; bass voices; a psalm of David’s.)
Save, Jehovah, because godly men have disappeared, because all is over with reliability among mankind.
They talk make-believes to each other, talk with slippery lips and double heart.
Jehovah will exterminate slippery lips, tongues that make great propositions,
Men that say “With our tongues we shall do bravely; we have our lips with us, who is sovereign over us?”
For violence to men in want, for needy men’s groaning, now I will stand up, says Jehovah, will set in salvation who pants for that.
Jehovah’s say is clean say, silver refined in a cupel on the ground, purified seven times.
You, Jehovah, will guard them, will keep them for this generation and forever.
Wrong-doers walk about on all sides when shabbiness stands high for mankind.
(Of the Director; a psalm of David’s.)
How long, Jehovah, will you perpetually forget? how long will you veil your face from me?
How long shall I house anxieties in my soul, have sorrow in my heart through the day? How long shall my enemies stand high over me?
Look at it, answer me, Jehovah, my God; give light to my eyes, that I may not sleep the sleep of death,
That my enemies may not say “I was too much for him,” my foes jubilate because I stagger,
when I have put my confidence in your friendship; Let my heart jubilate in your salvation,
let me sing to Jehovah because he has done me a good turn.
(Of the Director; of David’s.)
A rascal has said to himself “There is no God.” They behave viciously, abominably; there is nobody that does what is good.
Jehovah looked from the heavens upon mankind to see if there was a canny man, one that looked to God:
The whole lot had drawn off together, had degenerated, there was nobody that did what was good, not a single one.
Do all who perpetrate villainy not know? those who eat up my people eat bread, never call on Jehovah,—
There they are seized with terror, because God breaks up an ungodly man’s plan;
You shall put them to shame, because Jehovah has repudiated them.
O for Israel’s salvation coming from Sion! When Jehovah comes back to his people Jacob will jubilate, Israel make merry.
(A psalm of David’s.)
Jehovah, who will find a home in your tent, who reside on your sacred mountain?
One who walks conscientiously and does right and speaks truth in his heart.
He has not talked scandal, nor done an injury to his fellow, nor taken part in jeering at his neighbor.
He has no use for an immoral man, but those who fear Jehovah he honors. He swears to do a bad thing and does not substitute anything else;
he does not put out his money on interest Nor take a bribe against an innocent man. One who does these things will be unshaken forever.
(A mictam of David’s.)
Protect me, Jehovah, because I have taken refuge in you;
I have said to Jehovah my Lord “You are my good,
Counting out all holy ones that are on earth, grand ones that I have no fancy for.”
They get themselves many griefs; they hurry to get another god. I will not pour their libations of blood nor take their names on my lips.
Jehovah, you have apportioned my dish and my cup; you guide the falling of my lot.
Lines have fallen in pleasant places for me; Yes, and my estate has grown finer on my hands.
I will bless Jehovah, who has advised me; nights too my bosom instructs me.
I keep Jehovah always before me; because he is at my right hand I shall be unshaken.
So my heart is glad and my soul jubilant; my flesh too rests assured,
Because you will not leave my soul to the realm of death, will not give up the man of your friendship to see dissolution.
You will send me along paths of life; in your company there are joys in plenty, pleasant things are in your right hand perpetually.
(A prayer of David’s.)
Hear a just cause, Jehovah, listen to my appeal, give ear to my prayer not made with cheating lips.
From before you let judgment issue on my behalf; let your eyes take cognizance of equity.
You have tested me, examined me at night, assayed me; you will not find viciousness of mine; My mouth shall not pass over
for deeds of man. By the words of your lips I have kept from ruffian’s paths.
Steady my steps in your roads; let me not lose my footing.
I call to you, because you will answer me, God: bend your ear to me, hear my say.
Do acts of special friendship, you who by your right hand save from adversaries men who take refuge in you.
Guard me like the apple of your eye, screening me in the shadow of your wings,
From criminals who have assaulted me, my enemies who greedily surround me.
Their heart is tallow, their chest is blubber; they talk with a swagger.
They eye us, they surround us now, they fix their eyes on the country.
What he is like is a lion eager to make a kill, a two-year-old lion sitting in a covert.
Up, Jehovah, meet him face to face; put him down; preserve my life,
