And it will be better to Jehovah than a beast, a horned and hoofed steer.
See, humble men, and be glad; you who invoke God, and blithe be your hearts,
Because Jehovah is a hearer of needy men and does not disdain his prisoners.
Let sky and earth praise him, seas and everything that stirs in them,
Because God will save Sion, will rebuild the cities of Judah, and they shall live there and have possession of it,
And his servants’ issue shall take it as their estate and those who love his name shall people it.
(Of the Director; of David’s; for the memorial.)
Be pleased to deliver me, God; Jehovah, hasten to my help.
Let those be disappointed and abashed who are hunting after my life; Let those fall back and be humiliated who would like harm for me.
Let those stand aghast as they look back on their disappointment who are saying “Oho, oho!”
Let all who go in quest of you be joyous and merry in you; Let those who love your salvation say all the time “God is showing himself great!”
And me, insignificant and needy, make haste for me, God; You are my help and deliverer; my God, do not delay.
In you, Jehovah, I take refuge; forever let me not be disappointed.
In your right-doing deliver me and bring me through; turn your ear toward me and save me.
Be a citadel rock for me, a fastness house to save me, because you are my cliff and fastness.
My God, bring me off out of a wrong-doer’s hands, out of the clutch of an unscrupulous and unjust man.
For you are my hope, Lord; Jehovah has been my confidence from my childhood;
On you I have propped myself ever since my birth; it was you that severed me from my mother’s body; for you is my constant praise.
I rate like a miracle for many, and you are my sheltering refuge.
My mouth shall be filled with your praise and your magnificence all day.
Do not throw me away at the time of old age, when my strength gives out do not abandon me,
For my enemies are saying of me and those who watch for my life are conferring together,
Saying “God has abandoned him; give chase and catch him, for there is nobody to deliver him.”
God, do not be far off from me; my God, hasten to my help.
Let those who are adversaries to my life be disappointed, give out; let those who are looking for harm to me be wrapped in ignominy and humiliation.
But I will be always in expectation and be adding to all your praise;
My mouth shall tell the story of your right-doing and your salvation all day, For I do not know books,
I am bringing the Lord Jehovah’s exploits, I commemorate your right-doing, yours alone.
God, you have taught me since my childhood, and down to now I am telling your wonderful deeds;
And even to old age and gray hair, God, do not abandon me, Till I tell of your arm to a generation that is coming.
Your might and your right-doing, God, are most high, Forasmuch as you have done great things. God, who is like you?
You who have showed us distresses many and grievous will again bring us to life and again bring us up from the deeps of the earth.
Give me much greatness, comfort me more and more.
I on my part will give thanks to you, with a harp to your faithfulness, my God, Will make music for you with a lyre, Holy One of Israel.
My lips shall carol because I am making music for you, and my soul, which you have redeemed.
My tongue too all day shall deal with your right-doing, Because shamed are they, abashed are they, who seek harm for me.
(Of Solomon’s.)
God, give a king your justice, a king’s son your right-dealing!
He will give his verdicts to your people rightly and to your downtrodden justly.
Mountains shall carry peace for the people, and hills, by right.
He will do justice for downtrodden classes, will save sons of poverty, and will beat down a refuser of rights.
He shall last along with the sun, and before the moon for a cycle of generations.
He shall come down like rain on mowings, like showers drenching earth.
In his days right will flower and plentiful peace till there shall be no moon.
And he shall have the mastery from sea to sea and from the River to ends of earth.
Before him foes shall stoop and his enemies shall lick dust.
Kings of Spain and islands shall pay him tribute, kings of Sheba and Seba present gratuities,
And all kings shall do him reverence, all nations be subject to him.
For he shall deliver needy suppliant and downtrodden man and man whom none will help,
He shall have mercy on poor man and needy and save needy men’s lives,
From extortion and outrage he shall protect their lives, and deem their blood worth his attention,
That he may live and may be given gold from Sheba and that they may pray for him continually, may bless him all the day,
There may be plenty of grain in the country, shaking on mountaintops, His fruit may be like that of the Lebanon and the offspring of his body like the herbage of the earth.
Be his name forever, before the sun be his name set firm, And may they bless by him, all nations proclaim his happiness!
Blessed be Jehovah God, Israel’s God, who alone does wonders,
And blessed be his glorious name forever and be all the earth filled with his glory! Amen and amen!
End of the prayers of David the son of Jesse.
(A psalm of Asaph’s.)
Assuredly the Deity is good to the upright man, God to the single-hearted.
But as for me, my feet were very near going wrong, my steps were at the point of slipping,
Because I was jealous at reckless men, seeing the welfare of wrong-doers,
That they are under no duress, their paunch is sound and plump.
They are not in the troubles of humanity and are not stricken with mankind.
So pride is their necklace, a drapery of enormities wraps them round,
Their complexion is clearer than milk, they surpass the imagery of fancy.
They crack jokes over bad things and refuse justice in most lofty terms.
They have set their mouth in the sky and their tongue walks about on earth.
So his people turns back to this, and they are humiliated at the fullness of them
And say “How can it be that Deity knows and there is knowledge on high?
Here these are wrong-doers and forever undisturbed, they aggrandize their fortunes.
It was just to no purpose that I kept my heart clean and washed my hands in innocence,
And I have been smitten all day and my chastisement comes every morning.”
If I thought I would tell the story like that I should be faithless to the generation of your children.
And I studied to know about this; I found it a trying task
Till I went into Deity’s sanctuary, discerned their future:
You set their feet altogether in slippery places and bring them to their fall with blasting.
How they have become blighted wrecks in an instant, ended, totally gone in dissolution,
Like a dream that after waking is not there, at rousing you despise its images!
When my heart goes sour and I am pricked in my bosom,
I am brutish and do not know; I am a beast to you.
But I am always with you; you hold my right hand;
You will guide me on the line of your plan and afterward take me in glory.
Who is there for me in heaven? and beside you I care for nothing on earth.
My muscles and my brain are giving out, but God is my portion forever.
For those who are far from you do perish, you annihilate those who leave you and find an unlawful mate,
But to me God’s nearness is good; I have made the Lord Jehovah my refuge, telling the story of all your workings.
(Meditative; of Asaph’s.)
Why do you permanently repudiate us, God, why is your anger at the sheep you tended so smoking hot?
Remember your congregation you acquired of old, claimed as the tribe of your estate, The mountain of Sion on which you dwell,
which your footsteps have exalted to perpetual sublimity. An enemy has done everything bad to the holy things.
Your foemen roared like wild beasts within your meeting-place, set their ensigns as signs.
It shows like one who brings axes in upward into a thicket of wood,
And now they are battering its carvings one and all with ax and crowbar.
They have set fire to your sanctuary, desecrated the abode of your name down to the ground.
They said to themselves “We will overbear them one and all, will burn all meeting-places for divine service in the country.”
We have not seen our signs; there is no longer any prophet; we have nobody with us who knows how far it will go.
How long, God, shall a foe offer insults? Shall an enemy eternally treat your name with contempt?
Why do you draw back your hand and imprison your right hand in the fold of your robe?
But God is my King from of old, who does saving work in the midst of the earth.
It was you that by your might tore sea with convulsions and broke monsters’ heads to pieces over the water;
It was you that splintered Leviathan’s heads, giving him for food to the race of wildcats;
It was you that opened up spring and arroyo, it was you that dried out perennial rivers.
Yours is day, yours too is night; it was you that installed heavenly orb and sun.
It was you that set all the boundaries of earth; summer and winter it was you that framed.
Remember this; an enemy has been taunting Jehovah, an uncivilized people have treated your name with contempt.
Do not give up to wild beasts a soul that gives its thanks to you; do not permanently forget the life of your sufferers.
Look at your creatures filling with viciousness, for earth is the field of outrage.
Let a downtrodden man not come back humiliated; let a sufferer and a needy man praise your name.
Stand up, God, defend your rights! remember the insults you have had from rascals all day!
Do not forget the voice of your foemen, the hubbub of those who are out against you, that goes up all the time!
(Of the Director; “Do Not Spoil”; a psalm of Asaph’s, a song.)
We thank you, God, we thank you and call on your name, tell the story of your wonders.
“When my day comes I will judge evenhandedly.
Earth and all its inhabitants swing back and forth— I make its pillars fast. (Selah)
I say to reckless men ‘Do not be so reckless,’ and to wrong-doers ‘Do not carry your horns so loftily.’”
Do not carry your horns so very loftily, talking arrogance against the Rock;
For not from east nor from west nor yet from wilderness comes uplifting,
But God gives judgment, brings this one down and that one up.
For Jehovah has in his hand a cup with foaming wine full of strong spice, And he pours to this one and to that one; they are to drain its very dregs, all earth’s wrong-doers are to drink.
But I will exult forever, will make music to the God of Jacob,
And chop off all the horns of wrong-doers; right-doers’ horns shall be carried loftily.
(Of the Director; with string accompaniment; a psalm of Asaph’s; a song.)
Known in Judah is God, in Israel his name is great,
And he has his lodge in Salem and his dwelling in Sion.
There he broke quiver and bow, shield and sword and battalion. (Selah)
More grand and resplendent are you than mountains of prey.
Men of warlike heart were despoiled, lay sound asleep, and not any stalwart men could find their hands.
At your rebuke, God of Jacob, chariot and pony were in a trance.
Fearful are you, and who will stand his ground before you in your moment of anger?
From heaven you proclaimed a sentence; earth feared and was still
When God stood up for judgment to save all earth’s sufferers. (Selah)
For man’s rage pays homage to you, and the remnant from rage you gird up.
Vow and pay to your God Jehovah; all who live around him shall bring tribute to the Fearful.
He abates the spirits of potentates; he is fearful to the kings of earth.
(Of the Director over Jeduthun; of Asaph’s; a psalm.)
Aloud to God I cry, aloud to God that he may give ear to me.
In my day of distress I invoke the Lord, I spread out my hands. By night my soul drains out and never has its pain dulled, refuses to be comforted.
I remember God and am in a turmoil; I muse and my spirit fails me. (Selah)
My eyelids are held, I am oppressed and cannot speak.
I think over ancient days, remember years of old;
I wonder to myself in the night; I muse and make mental explorations:
Does the Lord repudiate us forever and ever, and will he never again be favorable?
Is his friendship permanently at an end, is all over with his loyalty, generation after generation?
Has Deity forgotten graciousness or shut up his sympathies in anger? (Selah)
And I thought of Jehovah’s being sick, of change in the right hand of the Most High.
I bring to mind Jehovah’s doings, because I remember out of ancient time your work of wonder,
And study over all your activities and muse on your deeds.
God, through the holy sphere is your course; who is so great a deity as God?
You are the Deity that did work of wonder, made your might known among the peoples.
With might and main you championed your people The sons of Jacob and Joseph. (Selah)
Water saw you, God, water saw you, winced, the deeps quavered too,
Clouds showered water, the heavens resounded, your arrows too flew about,
The sound of your thunder went like chariot-wheels, lightnings lighted up the world, earth quavered and quaked.
Your road was through the sea and your paths through a great water, and your footprints were not known.
You led your people along like a flock of sheep by the hands of Moses and Aaron.
(Meditative; of Asaph’s.)
Give ear to my instructions, my people, bend your ears to the say of my mouth.
I will open my mouth in a lesson of history, will stream mysterious facts from ancient time.
What we have heard and know and our fathers have told us
We will not conceal from their children, telling the tale to a later generation, Jehovah’s praises and his feats of might and the wonders that he did
And set up a testimony in Jacob and established a code of instructions in Israel Which he commanded our fathers to make known to their children,
In order that a later generation might know, children that were to be born, Might stand up and tell the story to their children,
to have them set their confidence in God And not forget Deity’s doings but keep his commandments,
And not be like their fathers, a stubborn and rebellious generation, A generation that had not set its heart firm and whose spirit was not loyal to Deity;
Sons of Ephraim who, archers armed, turned round on a day of combat.
They did not keep God’s covenant and refused to go by his instructions,
And forgot his deeds and his wonders that he had showed them.
Before their fathers he did wonderfully, in Egypt, the countryside of Soan.
He split a sea and brought them through, standing the water up as if in a heap,
And guided them by a cloud by day and at night by a light of fire.
He cracked open rocks in the wilderness and gave drink as abundant as the deeps,
And brought out a flow from a crag and made water come down like rivers.
But they went right on sinning against him, disobeying the Most High in the land of drought,
And had the thought of putting Deity on trial, asking for food for their appetites,
And talked at God, said “Can Deity set a table in the wilderness?
Here he has struck a rock and water ran out and arroyos ran in freshet, Can he give bread too or provide meat for his people?”
So Jehovah heard and was furious, and a fire broke out in Jacob and anger at Israel came up withal,
Because they did not have faith in God nor put their trust in his salvation;
And he gave orders to the heavens above and opened the doors of the sky,
And rained on them manna for food and gave them corn of heaven.
A man ate the bread of angels; he sent them all the provision they required.
He had an east wind set out in the sky, drove on a south wind by his power,
And rained meat on them like the soil they trod on and winged birds like the sand of the seas,
And let it fall within their camp, around their lodges,
And they ate and had every bit they could hold, and he brought them what they craved.
They were not cloyed from their craving, they still had their food in their mouths,
And God’s anger against them came up and he killed among their plumpest and brought down Israel’s young men.
With all this they still sinned and did not have faith in his wonders;
And he finished off their days with prostration and their years with palpitation.
If he killed them they invoked him, and came back in quest of Deity,
And remembered that God was their Rock and the Deity on high their Friend in need,
And cajoled him with their mouths and lied to him with their tongues,
But their hearts were not firmly with God and they were not loyal to his covenant.
But he is tenderhearted, purging away guilt and not dealing destruction, And does much of turning back his anger and does not stir up his ire,
And he remembered that they were mortals, a wind that goes and does not come back.
How often they disobeyed him in the wilderness, grieved him in desert land,
And put Deity on trial over again and brought regret to the Holy One of Israel!
They did not remember his hand, the day he redeemed them from distress,
Exhibited his tokens in Egypt and his miracles in the countryside of Soan,
And turned the branches of their Nile to blood, and their waters were undrinkable;
He sent among them ʽarob flies that ate them up and frogs that infested them;
He gave their growing things to the fall grasshoppers and what had come of their toil to the spring grasshoppers;
He killed their grapevines with hail and their sycamore trees with frost;
He handed their cattle over to the hail and their stock to the firebolts.
He let loose his anger upon them, wrath and hostility and belligerency, A sending of evil angels;
he saw to a path for his anger. He did not hold back their souls from death but handed their lives over to the pestilence,
And struck every eldest son in Egypt, the firstfruit of their powers in the homes of Ham,
And set his people in motion like so many sheep and drove them along in the wilderness like a flock,
And led them in secure confidence, they felt no dread, and the sea covered their enemies.
And he brought them into his sacred territory, that highland his right hand had gained,
And expelled nations before them and allotted them as definite estate, and settled in their homes the tribes of Israel.
But they put the Most High God on trial and disobeyed him, and did not keep to his lessons,
But fell away and were faithless like their fathers, turned over like an unreliable bow,
And provoked him with their heights and stirred his jealousy with their rock-carvings.
God heard and was furious and utterly spurned Israel,
And abandoned the tabernacle of Shiloh, the tent he had set up for presence among men,
And gave his power into captivity and his magnificence into the hands of a foe,
And handed his people over to the sword and was in wrath at his estate.
Fire consumed its young men and its maidens raised no death-song.
Its priests fell by the sword and its widows did not weep.
But the Lord woke up like one who had been asleep, like a champion who had been overcome by wine,
And drove his foes back, put them to perpetual ignominy,
And repudiated Joseph’s tent and did not choose the tribe of Ephraim,
But chose the tribe of Judah, Mount Sion which he loves,
And built his sanctuary like the peaks, like the earth whose foundations he has fixed forever,
And chose his servant David and took him from the work of the sheep,
Brought him from behind ewes in milk to shepherd his people Jacob and his estate Israel;
And he shepherded them with sincere heart and guided them with intelligent hands.
(A psalm of Asaph’s.)
Heathens have come into your estate, God, defiled your hallowed temple, laid Jerusalem in ruins.
They have given the bodies of your servants as food to the birds of the air, the flesh of your friends to the wild beasts of the earth.
They poured their blood out like water around Jerusalem and there was nobody to bury them.
We became the butt of our neighbors’ taunts, of the quips and gibes of those who live around us.
How long, Jehovah, will you be persistently angry, shall your jealousy burn like a fire?
Pour out your ire on the nations that do not know you and on kingdoms that have not called on your name,
For they have eaten Jacob up and desolated his ground.
Do not remember against us our former guilts; let your sympathy come in quickly for us, because we are in great want.
Help us, God of our salvation, in consideration for the honor of your name, and deliver us and purge our sins for your name’s sake.
Why should the nations say “Where is their God?” under our eyes let the vengeance for the shed blood of your servants be notable among the nations.
Let prisoners’ groaning come in before you; with your so great arm release men under sentence of death;
And return to our neighbors seven times over into their bosoms the insults they have offered to you, Lord;
And we, your people, the sheep you tend, will give you thanks forever, will tell of your praise to generation after generation.
(Of the Director; to “Lilies a testimony”; of Asaph’s; a psalm.)
Shepherd of Israel, give ear, you who guide Joseph along like a drove of sheep; You who are seated on the cherubs, beam out
before Ephraim and Benjamin and Manasseh, Stir your might and come for salvation for us.
Bring us back, God, and show a shining face, and let us be saved.
Jehovah, God, Armies, till when are you smoking hot at your people’s prayer,
Feeding them tear-bread and giving them tears to drink by the gallon?
You are making us an object for our neighbors’ quarrels, and our enemies amuse themselves with us.
Bring us back, God, Armies, and show a shining face, and let us be saved.
You move a grapevine out of Egypt, dislodge nations and set it out,
Clear the ground before it and get it rooted, and it fills the country;
Mountains are covered with its shadow, mighty cedars with its branches;
It is running its canes to the sea and its shoots to the River;
Why is it you have breached its fences and everybody that comes along the road is picking at it,
Hogs out of the badlands are eating it off, and beasts of the range are browsing on it?
God, Armies, come back, look from heaven and see,
And care for this vine and put it in order, what your right hand planted, and the son you appropriated to yourself.
They have burned it down, lopped it off; let them perish at the rebuke of your face.
Let your hand be on the man of your right hand and the son of man you appropriated to yourself,
And we will not fall back from you; bring us to life, and we will call on your name.
Jehovah, God, Armies, bring us back; show a shining face, and let us be saved.
(Of the Director; to the Gittith. Of Asaph’s.)
Shout for God our strength, cheer for Jacob’s God!
Strike up music and sound tambourine, dulcet lyre with harp,
Blow the ram-horn at the new moon, at the full, on the day of our feast.
For that is an institution of Israel’s, a due of Jacob’s God.
He made it a commemoration in Joseph when he went out over Egypt. I heard a lip I had not known,
“I let his shoulder turn away from the load; his hands shall pass the basket by;
You called in distress, and I have rescued you. I will answer you through a screen of thunder; I will test you at a water of dispute. [Selah]
Listen, my people, and let me testify to you; Israel, if you will listen to me,
Have no strange deity among you and not do reverence to any foreign deity,
I Jehovah am your God, who am bringing you up out of Egypt; open your mouth wide and I will fill it.
But does my people not listen to my voice, will Israel not have me,
I will turn them loose to their willful wicked way; they shall go by their own contrivances.
If my people did listen to me, Israel did go my ways,
Readily would I humble their enemies and bring my hand back against their foes.
Those who hate Israel should cringe to him and their disaster be forever.
I would feed him out of the richest of wheat and give you out of rocks your fill of honey.”
(A psalm of Asaph’s.)
God stands in the divine convention, pronounces judgment in the midst of gods.
“How long will you judge unfairly, show favor to wrong-doers? (Selah)
Give judgment for poor man and orphan; allow a downtrodden and impoverished man to be in the right.
Preserve a poor and needy man; deliver him from wrong-doers’ hands.
They do not know; they do not perceive; they walk in the dark; all earth’s foundations give way.
I thought you were gods, and sons of the Most High all of you;
But you shall die like human beings, fall like any grandees.”
Rise, God; judge the earth; for you are liege lord over all the nations.
(A song; a psalm of Asaph’s.)
Do not take repose, God; do not be deaf, Deity, nor quiet,
Because here are your enemies making an uproar, your haters raising their heads,
Conspiring in an artful plot against your people and consulting over a policy against the objects of your protection.
They say “come on, we will efface their nationality and the name of Israel shall not be remembered anymore.”
For they have come to a unanimous agreement, formed a league against you,
The tents of Edom and the Ishmaelites, Moab and the Hagarites,
Gebal and ʽAmmon and ʽAmalek, Philistia with the inhabitants of Tyre.
Assyria has joined them too, they have reinforced the sons of Lot. [Selah]
Do to them as you did to Midian, to Sisera, to Jabin, at Kishon Arroyo,
That were annihilated at ʽEn-Dor, that became manure for the soil.
Make them, their nobles, like Raven and like Wolf, like Zebah and Salmunnaʽ all their dukes,
Those who have said “Let us take God’s meadows for our possession.”
My God, make them like a tumbleweed, like straw before a wind;
Like a fire burning out a brush-patch or a conflagration blazing over mountains,
So you will chase them with your tempest and drive them in consternation by your gale.
Fill their faces with disgrace that they may seek out your name, Jehovah,
May have unending shame and consternation and be abashed and perish,
And know it is you alone that are named Jehovah, on high over all the earth.
(Of the Director; to the Gittith; of the sons of Korah; a psalm.)
How lovable your dwelling-places are, Jehovah of Armies!
My soul yearns, yes, breaks down with its eagerness for Jehovah’s courts; my heart and flesh shout toward living Deity.
Even a little bird has found a house, and a swallow a nest for herself, That has placed her brood by your altars, Jehovah of Armies, my King and my God.
Happy those who live at your house; they will keep praising you. (Selah)
Happy are men who have strength in you, who have highways at heart,
Those who pass through Baca Vale making it a region of springs, even pools that fall rain overspreads.
They go on from good times to good times; Deity, God, is to be seen at Sion.
Jehovah, God, Armies, hear my prayer; [Selah] give ear, God of Jacob:
See our shield, God, and look at the face of your anointed.
For a day in your courts is better than a thousand; I had rather be at the threshold of the house of my God than lodge in tents of wickedness.
For our God Jehovah is a sun and shield; Jehovah will give grace and glory, will not withhold good from those who go by a good conscience.
Jehovah of Armies, happy the man that puts confidence in you.
(Of the Director; of the sons of Korah; a psalm.)
You took your country into favor, Jehovah, came back to Jacob,
Pardoned your people’s guilt, covered up all their sin, [Selah]
Drew back all your wrath, put a stop to your anger.
Come back to us, God of our salvation, and suppress your vexation at us.
Will you be angry with us forever, carry your anger on from generation to generation?
Will not you, you, again bring us to life and let your people be glad in you?
Show us your friendship, Jehovah, giving us your salvation.
I will hear what the Deity Jehovah will speak, for he will speak peace to his people and the objects of his friendship and to those who turn their hearts back to him.
All near for those who fear him is his salvation, for glory to dwell in our country,
Friendliness and loyalty having met, right and peace having kissed,
Loyalty springing up from the earth and right looking out from the sky,
Jehovah too giving goodness and our earth giving its growth,
Right going before him and salvation by the road he treads.
(A prayer of David’s.)
Bend your ear, Jehovah, answer me, because I am unhappy and needy.
Preserve my life, because I am a man of your friendship; save your servant who puts his trust in you.
You are my God; be gracious to me, because I call to you all day.
Gladden your servant’s soul, because it is on you, Lord, that I count.
For you, Lord, are kind and forgiving and of great friendship to all who call on you.
Give ear to my prayer, Jehovah; listen to my suppliant voice;
In my day of distress I call to you because you will answer me.
There is no one like you among the gods, Lord, and there are not the like of your deeds.
All nations that you have made shall come and do reverence before you, Lord, and glorify your name,
Because you are great and doer of wonders, you alone are God.
Show me your road, Jehovah; I will go by your truth; unite my heart to fear your name.
I will give you thanks, my Lord, my God, with all my heart, and glorify your name forever,
Because your friendliness is great toward me and you deliver my life from the bottom of the realm of death;
For high-handed men stood up against me and a company of overbearing men were looking for my life and had not set you before them,
But you, Lord, are a deity tenderhearted and kindly, patient and very friendly and loyal.
Turn toward me and be gracious to me; give your shelter to your servant and save your bondwoman’s son.
Do by me a token of good, that those who hate me may see, and be disappointed, that you, Jehovah, have helped me and comforted me.
(Of the sons of Korah; a psalm; a song.)
His foundation on sacred mountains
Jehovah loves, the gates of Sion more than all the abodes of Jacob.
Glorious things are to be spoken of you, city of God! (Selah)
I will mention Rahab and Babylon for those who know me; here are Philistia and Tyre, with Nubia, this one was born there.
But of Sion it shall be said “Man upon man was born in her,” and he, the Most High, holds her fast.
Jehovah will count in the register of peoples “This one was born there.” (Selah)
And singers as well as dancers will all shout of you.
(A song; a psalm of the sons of Korah; of the Director; to “Mahalath”; for intonation; meditative, of Heman the Ezrahite’s.)
Jehovah, my God, I clamor by day, I cry in your presence by night.
Let my prayer come before you, bend your ear to my appeal,
Because my soul has its fill of evils and my being is touching the realm of the shades,
I rank as down in the Pit, I have become like a man beyond assistance,
Free among the dead, like stabbed men, men lying in graves, Whom you no longer remember, they being sundered from your hand;
You have laid me in the bottom of the Pit, in depths of darkness and abysses of ooze.
On me your ire rests its weight and you have brought in all your breakers. (Selah)
You have taken my acquaintances far away from me, made me an object of abhorrence to them, Shut up so that I cannot get out;
my eye has grown hopeless with misery. I have called to you, Jehovah, every day, have laid my hands out toward you.
Will you do wonders for the dead, or will shades stand up and give you thanks? (Selah)
Will your friendliness be told of in the grave, your faithfulness in the land of the gone forever?
Will your wonders be made known in the darkness and your right-doing in the land of forgottenness?
But I, Jehovah, clamor to you and in the morning my prayer presents itself to you.
Why do you disown my soul, Jehovah, veil your face from me?
From a child I have been wretched and worn, have carried your terrors, been unnerved,
Your blasts of anger have swept over me, your overwhelmings have annihilated me,
They have swept around me like water all day, united to hem me in.
You have taken lover and friend far away from me, my acquaintances are darkness—
(Meditative; of Ethan the Ezrahite’s.)
Jehovah’s acts of friendship I will forever sing; to generation after generation I will announce your faithfulness with my mouth,
Because you have said “Forever shall friendship be built up”; in the skies you set your faithfulness firm.
“I have covenanted to my chosen one, sworn to my servant David,
‘To all time I will set your posterity firm and build your throne to generation after generation’”; [Selah]
And heaven shall acknowledge your wonders, Jehovah, your faithfulness too, in the assembly of holy ones.
For who in highest heaven is to be matched with Jehovah, to be compared to Jehovah among the sons of deities?
A fearful Deity in the council of the holy ones, great and terrible over all who are around him.
Jehovah, God of Armies, who is like you? sturdy is Jehovah; and your faithfulness is around you.
You rule over the pride of the sea; when its waves toss you still them.
You felled Rahab as if he were stabbed through; with your arm of might you dispersed your enemies.
Yours is sky, yours too is earth; the world and all that fills it you founded.
North and south you created; Tabor and Hermon warble your name.
Arm you have, and vigor withal; your hand is strong, your right hand high.
Right dealing and just judgment are the base of your throne; friendship and loyalty come forward in your presence.
Happy the people that know resounding cheers of praise; they will walk in the shining of your face, Jehovah,
They will jubilate all day in your name and exalt your right-doing,
Because you are the grandeur of their might and by your acceptance you raise our horn aloft.
For to Jehovah belongs our shield and to the Holy One of Israel our king.
You then spoke in a vision to the man of your friendship and said “I have laid help upon a champion, have taken up a chosen one out of the people,
Have found my servant David, have anointed him with my sacred oil,
With whom my hand shall be firm, yes, my arm shall brace him.
No enemy shall hold him in peonage nor man of foul play grind him down,
But I will pound up his foes before him and defeat those who hate him,
And he shall have with him my faithfulness and friendship, and by my name he shall carry his horn high,
And I will lay his hand on the sea and his right hand on the rivers.
He shall call to me ‘You are my Father, my Deity and the Rock of my salvation’;
I withal will make him my firstborn, on high over the kings of earth.
I will keep my friendship to him forever and my covenant to him shall be loyal,
And I will make his posterity last for aye and his throne like the time of the sky.
If his sons abandon my instructions and do not go by my laws,
If they disregard my rules and do not keep my commandments,
I will punish their crime with a cudgel and their guilt with blows,
But not cancel my friendship with him nor forswear my faithfulness.
I will not disregard my covenant nor change what has gone out of my lips.
One thing I have sworn by my holiness, I will not lie to David,
His posterity shall be forever and his throne like the sun before me,
Like the moon, secured ever and aye, faithful in the ether.” (Selah)
But you have repudiated and rejected, been infuriated with your anointed one,
Ignored the covenant with your servant, dropped his diadem desecrated on the ground,
Breached all his fences, laid his fortifications in ruin.
All passersby pillage him; he has become a butt for his neighbors’ insults.
You let his foes’ right hand go high, you gladden all his enemies.
You turn back his sword-blade too, and do not let him stand up in battle.
You have made an end of his brightness, hurled his throne to the ground,
Shortened his time of youth, wrapped him in shame. (Selah)
How long, Jehovah, will you persistently veil yourself, shall your choler burn like a fire?
Remember, Lord, what vitality is, in what unsubstantiality you created all mankind;
What man is to live and never see death, get his life clear of the grasp of the grave? (Selah)
Where are your first acts of friendship, Lord? You swore to David by your faithfulness!
Remember, Lord, the insults to your servant, my pocketing all animosities from peoples,
How your enemies have been insulting, Jehovah, been throwing insults at your anointed one’s heels.
Blessed be Jehovah forever. Amen and amen.
(A prayer; of Moses the man of God.)
Lord, you have been citadel of ours in generation upon generation.
Before mountains were born or earth and universe came to the pangs of birth, And from eternity to eternity, you are Deity.
You send a man back into the clods and say “Back again, sons of mankind!”
(For a thousand years are to your eyes like a yesterday when it is going by or a watch in the night.)
You wash them away; they are sleep. In the morning they make a fresh start like grass;
In the morning it is blooming and fresh; at evening it is wilted and dried out.
For we are all gone at your anger, and we are struck with sudden death at your ire.
You have set our offenses where they confront you, in the illumination of your face what we had kept dark.
For all our days shrink back at your wrath, we finish off our years like a sigh.
The time we do our sleeping in is seventy years or, with a strong constitution, eighty years, And its swaggering is fuss and futility, for it goes by in a rush and we take wing.
Who knows the formidableness of your anger, and who has seen the oppressiveness of your wrath?
To count off our days teach us aright, that we may get a heart of wisdom in.
Come back, Jehovah—when? and change your mind as to your servants.
Give us your friendship amply in the morning, so that we may carol and make merry throughout our days.
Give us as many days of gladness as you have given of hardship, as many years as we have been seeing disaster.
Let your activity be apparent toward your servants and your grandeur over their sons,
And may the graciousness of the Lord our God be over us; and give firmness to the work of our hands.
One who lives under the Most High’s screen, lodges under Shaddai’s canopy,
Who calls Jehovah “my refuge and fastness, my God in whom I trust”—
For he will deliver you from fowler’s trap, from threats of malice;
He will overarch you with his pinions and under his wings you shall take refuge; great shield and castle is his loyalty.
You shall not fear nighttime horror, arrow flying by day,
Pestilence walking in murky blackness, fatality making havoc at noon;
A thousand shall fall at your side and ten thousand at your right hand, but it shall not come up to you;
You shall only look on with your eyes and see the retribution of wrong-doers,
Because you have Jehovah for your refuge, have made the Most High your citadel.
No harm will come upon you nor blight draw near your home,
Because he will give his angels orders for you, to guard you in all your courses;
They shall take you up in their hands to keep you from stubbing your toe on a stone.
You shall tread on lion and viper, trample down two-year-old lion and reptile.
Because he is in love with me I will see him through, will set him out of reach of harm because he knows my name.
He shall call on me and I will answer him; I am with him in distress, I will rescue him and show him honor.
Of long life I will give him his fill, and will let him feast his eyes on my salvation.
(A psalm; a sabbath-day song.)
It is good to give thanks to Jehovah and make music to your name, Most High,
To tell your friendship in the morning and your faithfulness in the nights
With ten-string and with harp, with harmony on a lyre,
Because you have gladdened me, Jehovah, by what you have done; over the works of your hands I carol.
How great are your works, Jehovah! very deep are your thoughts.
A stupid man will not know, nor a fool see into this:
When wrong-doers burgeon like weeds and all villains bloom It is so that they may be rooted out once for all;
but you are enthroned aloft forever, Jehovah.
For there do your enemies, Jehovah, there do your enemies perish; all villains are splintered apart;
And you have given me a high horn like a ure’s, have bedewed me with fresh oil,
And caused my eyes to look on at the fate of my ill-wishers, my ears to hear of the fate of those who stood up against me.
A right-doer will bud like a palm tree, grow tall like a cedar on the Lebanon;
Set out at Jehovah’s house, they will grow full of branches in the courts of our God,
Will be still fruitful in old age, will be lush and verdant,
Announcing that straightforward is Jehovah, my Rock, and there is no cheating about him.
Jehovah is king; Jehovah has put on, has put on majesty, has belted himself with might, has established the world too, not to be disturbed.
Your throne is firm since ancient times; your being is from eternity.
Rivers raised, Jehovah, rivers raised their voices, rivers were dashing high.
Above the sounds of great water, more grand than breakers of sea, more grand is Jehovah aloft.
Your lessons are most trustworthy; its holiness is glory for your house, Jehovah, for the length of time.
Deity of vengeance, Jehovah, Deity of vengeance, beam out!
Uplift yourself, Judge of the earth, send back retribution upon proud men.
How long shall wrong-doers, Jehovah, how long shall wrong-doers jubilate?
They stream out arrogant talk, and villains have plenty to say,
They beat down your people, Jehovah, and wear down your estate,
Kill widow and immigrant and murder orphans;
And they think “Jehovah does not see and the Holy One of Israel does not take it in.”
Take this in, stupid ones among the people; and you fools, when will you be sensible?
Is he who planted ears not to hear and he who shaped eyes not to take a look?
Is the instructor of nations to do no correcting, he who teaches man to know?
Jehovah knows man’s thoughts, how windy they are.
Happy the man whom you discipline, Jehovah, and teach out of your code,
To give him quietness out of days of evil till a pitfall is dug for the wrong-doer;
For Jehovah will not abandon his people nor forsake his estate.
For judgment will come back to doing the right, and this will all the honest-hearted follow.
Who will stand up for me against evil-doers, who take his stand for me against perpetrators of villainy?
If Jehovah had not been a help to me my soul was almost finding its dwelling in the land of silence.
If I think my foot is slipping your friendship, Jehovah, steadies me.
When I have in my bosom many cogitations your comforts afford me pleasure.
Is a throne of malignity associated with you, one that frames mischief into a rule of law?
They raid a right-doer’s life and condemn innocent blood.
But Jehovah has been a fastness to me and my God my rock of refuge,
And has turned their villainy back upon themselves, and will annihilate them in their wickedness; our God Jehovah will annihilate them.
Come, let us shout for Jehovah, raise a cheer for our Rock of salvation,
Let us come into his presence with thanksgiving, raise a cheer for him with music,
Because Jehovah is a great Deity and a great King over all gods,
He in whose hand are the most secluded parts of earth, and the peaks of mountains are his;
He to whom the sea belongs, and who made it, and whose hands formed dry land.
Come in, let us bow low and do reverence, let us kneel before our maker Jehovah,
Because he is our God and we are the people he pastures and the sheep of his hand. Today, if you will obey him,
Do not stiffen your hearts as at Meribah, as on the day of Massah in the wilderness,
When your fathers tried me out, tested me and saw what I did.
Forty years I felt the loathsomeness of that generation and said “They are a people of erring hearts, not knowing my courses,”
So that I swore in my anger they should not come into my rest.
Sing a new song for Jehovah; sing for Jehovah, all the earth!
Sing for Jehovah, bless his name, tell the good news of his salvation day after day,
Tell the tale of his glory among the nations, among all the peoples his wondrous feats,
Because Jehovah is great and high-praised; he is terrible over all gods,
For all the peoples’ gods are trumperies, but Jehovah made the skies.
Majesty and splendor are before him, might and magnificence in his sanctuary.
Give to Jehovah, clans of peoples, give to Jehovah glory and might!
Give to Jehovah the glory that belongs to his name; carry an offering and come into his courts.
Do reverence to Jehovah in stately sacred garb; tremble before him, all the earth.
Say among the nations “Jehovah is king, has established the world too, not to be disturbed, will give fair verdicts for peoples.”
Let the heavens be glad and the earth jubilant, let the sea and what fills it thunder,
Let fields and everything in them exult, then let all trees on the rocks shout,
Before Jehovah, because he has come, because he has come to judge the earth! He will judge the world aright and peoples faithfully.
Jehovah is king! let the earth be jubilant, many coasts be glad!
Clouds and thick air are around him, right and justice are the base of his throne.
A fire goes before him and burns off his foes on every side.
His lightnings light up the world; the earth sees and trembles.
Mountains melt down like wax before Jehovah, before the Lord of all the earth.
The sky tells his right-doing, and all the peoples see his glory.
All statue-worshipers shall be put to shame, those who glory in trumpery deities; do reverence to him, all gods!
Sion hears and is glad, and Judah’s daughters are jubilant, for your judgments, Jehovah,
Because you, Jehovah, are on high over all the earth, high far above all gods.
Jehovah loves those who hate evil, guards the lives of the men of his friendship, delivers them from the hands of wrong-doers.
Light rises for the right-doer and gladness for men of honest heart.
Be glad in Jehovah, right-doers, and give thanks at the remembrance of his holiness.
(A psalm.)
Sing a new song for Jehovah, for he has done wondrous things; His right hand and his holy arm have brought his salvation.
Jehovah has made his salvation known, unveiled his right-doing before the eyes of the nations.
He has remembered his friendship and faithfulness to Israel’s house; all earth’s extremities have seen our God’s salvation.
Raise cheers for Jehovah, all the earth, break out and shout and make music;
Make music for Jehovah with lyre, with lyre and sound of minstrelsy;
With trumpets and sound of ram-horn give ringing blasts before the King, Jehovah!
Let the sea and what fills it thunder, the world and its inhabitants,
Let rivers clap their hands, mountains shout together,
Before Jehovah, because he has come to judge the earth; he will judge the world aright and peoples uprightly.
Jehovah is king! let peoples quake! he is enthroned on cherubs; let the earth swing!
Jehovah is great in Sion, and lofty is he over all the peoples.
Let them praise your name as great and terrible. Holy is he.
And royal might loves justice; you have set uprightness firm; you have done the just and right thing by Jacob.
Exalt our God Jehovah and do reverence at his footstool; holy is he.
Moses and Aaron among his priests and Samuel among those who call on his name Called to Jehovah and he answered them;
in a pillar of cloud he spoke to them; They heard his lessons, and an institution he gave them.
Jehovah, our God, you did answer them, You were to them a pardoning Deity and one who took vengeance for their misbehavior.
Exalt our God Jehovah and do reverence at his sacred mountain, for holy is our God Jehovah!
(A psalm for thanksgiving.)
Raise cheers for Jehovah, all the land,
worship Jehovah with gaiety, come in before him with shouting;
Know that Jehovah is God, he made us and his are we, his people and the sheep of his pasturing.
Enter his gates with thanksgiving, his courts with praise, give him thanks and bless his name,
Because good is Jehovah; his friendship is forever and his faithfulness to generation after generation.
(Of David’s; a psalm.)
Friendliness and justice I sing; to you, Jehovah, I make music.
I will consider a faultless course; when will you come to me? I will walk with a steady heart within my house.
I will not lay a base proposition under my eyes. Doing unprincipled things I hate, it shall not be my habit.
A crooked heart I will eschew, will have no knowledge of evil.
One who covertly defames another I will annihilate. A man of lofty eyes and domineering heart I will not stand.
I will have my eyes out for earth’s reliable men to live with me. One who walks a faultless course, he shall serve me.
One who practices fraud shall not have a seat inside my house. A liar shall not hold a footing under my eyes.
Morning by morning I will annihilate all earth’s wrong-doers, Exterminating from Jehovah’s city all who commit villainy.
(Prayer of a man in misery when he is fainting away and pours out his complaint before Jehovah.)
Jehovah, hear my prayer and let my clamor come in to you.
Do not veil your face from me on the day I am in distress; bend your ear to me; on the day when I call answer me speedily;
For my days have gone off in smoke and my bones are charring like fuel.
My heart is slashed down and dried out like weeds, for I have forgotten eating my food.
By the sound of my moaning my bones stick to my flesh.
I am like a wilderness barn-owl, I am the same as little owls in wasted sites.
I am watchful and uneasy like a bird alone on a roof.
All day my enemies taunt me, those who go wild against me make an oath of me,
Because I have been eating ashes like bread and mixing my gulps of drink with weeping
Because of your hostility and wrath, because you have taken me up and thrown me down.
My days stoop like a shadow and I dry out like weeds.
But you, Jehovah, are enthroned forever, and the remembrance of you is for generation after generation.
You will stand up and take pity on Sion when it is time to be gracious to her, when a date comes,
Because your servants value her stones and have a regard for her earth,
That nations may fear Jehovah’s name and all the kings on earth your glory
Because Jehovah has rebuilt Sion, has appeared in his glory,
Has turned toward the prayer of the destitute and not despised their prayer.
This shall be written down for a later generation, and a people that is to be created shall praise Jehovah
Because he has looked out from his holy place aloft, Jehovah from heaven has looked at earth,
Hearing a prisoner’s groans, unchaining men sentenced to death,
That Jehovah’s fame may be told of in Sion and his praise at Jerusalem
When peoples gather together, and kingdoms, to worship Jehovah.
He has worn down my strength on the road, has shortened my days;
I say “My God, do not lift me away at half my days; your years are through a generation of generations.
You laid earth’s foundations before, and heaven is the work of your hands;
They will perish, but you will stand; and they will all wear out like a garment, Like a dress you will change them and changed they will be,
but you are yourself and there will be no end of your years.
Your worshipers’ sons shall live in their homes, and their descendants shall stand fast before you.”
(Of David’s.)
Bless Jehovah, my soul; all my being, through and through, bless his holy name!
Bless Jehovah, my soul, and do not forget all he has done for you,
He who forgives all your guilt, who cures all your diseases,
Who protects your life from being swallowed up in the depths below, who crowns you with his friendship and sympathy,
Who satisfies your lifetime with good things, letting you renew your youth like the great vulture.
Jehovah does things that are right, and acts of justice for those to whom it is denied.
He makes his courses known to Moses, his doings to the sons of Israel.
Tenderhearted and kindly is Jehovah, patient and very friendly.
He will not keep up a contention permanently nor lay up a score forever.
He has not done to us things to match our sins nor treated us in accordance with our guilt,
For like the height of sky over earth is the transcendence of his friendship over those who fear him.
As far away as east from west has he put our crimes from us.
Like a father’s tenderness for sons is Jehovah’s for those who fear him,
Because he knows our structure, remembers that we are clay.
Man’s lifetime is like that of grass; like field flowers, so does he bloom;
For a wind passes through and he is not there, and his place is no longer aware of him.
But Jehovah’s friendship is from eternity to eternity over those who fear him, and his fair dealing to sons of sons,
To those who keep his covenant and who remember his mandates, living up to them.
Jehovah has set his throne fast in the heavens, and his kingdom rules everything.
Bless Jehovah, you angels of his, formidable in strength, doers of his bidding, obeyers of his word!
Bless Jehovah, all you legions of his, servitors of his, doers of his pleasure!
Bless Jehovah, all works of his in all the places under his sway! Bless Jehovah, my soul!
Bless Jehovah, my soul! Jehovah, my God, you are great indeed; in majesty and splendor you are robed,
You who wrap light about you like a cloak, who stretch sky like a curtain;
Who frame your upper stories in water, make clouds your carriage, go about on wings of wind;
Who make winds your messengers, blazing fires your servitors;
Who set earth on its foundations, nevermore to be unsettled,
Covered it with the deep as if with a robe, water standing above mountains—
At your rebuke the water takes flight, at the sound of your thunder it makes off in haste,
Mountains come up, vales go down to the place you have founded for them,
You have fixed a boundary it is not to cross, not to come back to cover the earth;
You who let out springs in the arroyos to run between mountains,
To water all beasts of the wilds, for wild asses to slake their thirst,
For birds of the air to perch over, sounding their notes amid the leaves;
You who water mountains out of your lofts so that the earth has its fill of the fruit of your work,
Who make grass grow for the cattle and vegetation for man’s labor, Bringing out bread from the earth
and letting wine make a man’s heart merry, Brightening faces with oil and letting bread brace a man up,
Letting wild trees have their fill, cedars of Lebanon that you planted,
Where birds nest, storks have their homes in their tops,
Ibexes have highest mountains, dassies have crags for a refuge;
Who have made a moon to mark dates, a sun that knows its setting;
You cause darkness, and there is night, in which all creatures of the bush steal about,
The two-year-old lions roar for prey and to seek their food from Deity;
The sun rises, they take cover and lie down in their dens,
Man goes out to his activities and to his labors till evening.
How manifold are your works, Jehovah, all of which you have made with wisdom! the earth is filled with your creations.
Here is the sea, great and wide, and in it numberless forms of moving life, tiny animals with great ones;
Ships travel there; Leviathan, that you formed to play in it.
They all rely on you, Jehovah, to give their food at the due time.
You give to them, they pick up; you open your hand, they have their fill of good things;
You veil your face, they are struck with sudden death; you take up their spirits, they expire and go back to their clay.
You loose your spirit, they are created and you make new the surface of the soil.
May Jehovah’s glory be forever, may Jehovah be gladdened in his works,
He who looks at the earth and it shivers, touches the mountains and they smoke.
I will sing for Jehovah while I live, make music for my God while I exist.
May my meditations be sweet to him; may I be glad in Jehovah.
May sinners come to an end out of the earth and wrong-doers no longer exist. Bless Jehovah, my soul!
Praise Jehovah! Thank Jehovah, proclaim his name, make known among the peoples his deeds;
Sing for him, make music for him, review all his wonders,
Boast of his holy name; let the hearts of those who seek Jehovah be glad.
Look to Jehovah and his strength; always be looking for his face.
Remember his wonders that he has done, his miracles and the judgments of his mouth,
You descendants of his servant Abraham, sons of his chosen one Jacob.
He is our God Jehovah, his judgments run throughout the earth.
Forever he remembers his covenant, a word that he has ordained for a thousand years,
Which he undertook with Abraham, and Isaac had his oath,
And he confirmed it to be a decree for Jacob, a perpetual covenant for Israel,
“To you I will give Canaan as your definite estate,”
When they were few in number, a mere handful, and immigrants in it,
And going about from nation to nation, from a kingdom to another people.
He did not let men deny them justice, but reproved kings on their account,
“Do not touch my anointed ones nor harm my prophets.”
And he called down a famine upon the country, broke every bread-stock;
He sent a man before them; Joseph was sold for a slave;
They hobbled his feet with shackles, his life was locked in iron,
Till the time when his word came true, Jehovah’s say showed his metal,
A king sent and undid him, a ruler of peoples and released him,
Appointed him lord of his household, ruler over all his means,
To dictate to his generals at will and tutor his statesmen;
And Israel came into Egypt and Jacob lived as an immigrant in the country of Ham,
And he made his people very prolific and they outmultiplied their foes.
He turned their hearts to hate his people, to plot against his servants;
He sent his servant Moses, Aaron whom he chose;
They set out the words of his tokens among them, and miracles in the country of Ham.
He sent darkness, and dark it grew; and they did not disobey his words.
He turned their water to blood and brought their fishes to death.
Their country swarmed with frogs in the chambers of their kings.
He gave the word, and ʽarob flies came in; mosquitoes, in all their territory.
He let their showers be hail, flaming fire in their country,
And struck down their grapevine and fig-tree and smashed the trees of their territory.
He gave the word, and grasshoppers came, locusts innumerable,
And ate off all plant life in their country and ate off the fruit of their soil.
And he struck down every eldest son in their country, firstfruits of all their powers.
And he brought them out with silver and gold, with no one among his tribes stumbling;
Egypt was glad of their going out, because the dread of them had fallen upon them.
He spread out a cloud for a screen and a fire to give light at night;
They asked, and he brought quails and gave them full meals of sky-bread;
He opened a rock and water gushed out, a river ran in the parched wastes;
Because he remembered his holy word with his servant Abraham.
And he brought his people out with rejoicing, his chosen ones with shouting,
And gave them nations’ lands, and they took possession of what folk upon folk had toiled for,
To the end that they might observe his institutions and keep the rules of his code. Praise Jehovah!
Praise Jehovah! Thank Jehovah, because he is good, because his friendship lasts forever.
Who shall put Jehovah’s feats into words, voice all his praise?
Happy are those who observe laws, who do what is right at every time.
Remember me, Jehovah, in the favor you show to your people, take care of me in your salvation,
For me to have the sight of the good your chosen ones get, to be glad in the gladness of your nation, to make my boast with your estate.
We have sinned with our fathers, have done perversely, wrongly.
Our fathers in Egypt did not appreciate your wonders, Did not remember how many your acts of friendship had been, and disobeyed the Most High at the Red Sea.
But he saved them for the honor of his name, to make known his prowess,
And rebuked the Red Sea, and it dried off, and he marched them through the deeps as if through the wilderness,
And saved them out of the hands of one who hated them, and reclaimed them out of an enemy’s hand,
And water covered their foes, not one of them was left;
And they believed his words and sang his praise.
They were quick to forget his works, would not wait for his plan,
But gave way to a craving in the wilderness and put Deity on trial in desert land;
And he gave them what they asked but sent sickness into their systems.
And they grew jealous of Moses in the camp, of Aaron, the one holy to Jehovah;
Earth opened and swallowed Dathan and covered Abiram’s company,
And a fire broke out in their company, flame set wrong-doers ablaze.
They made a calf at Horeb and did reverence to a bronze statue,
And changed their glory for a figure of a grass-eating bull;
They forgot the Deity who had saved them, had done great things in Egypt,
Wonderful things in the country of Ham, terrible things at the Red Sea.
And he thought of exterminating them, had it not been that Moses his chosen one Stood in the breach before him to turn back his ire from working ruin.
And they refused a delectable country, would not believe his word
But found fault in their tents, did not obey Jehovah,
And he pledged himself against them to have them fall in the wilderness
And to scatter their descendants among the nations and disperse them through the countries.
And they fraternized with the Baal of Peghor and ate sacrifices to dead things,
And gave provocation by their misbehavior, and a plague broke out among them;
Pinehas stood firm and intervened, and the plague was checked,
And it was credited to him for righteousness generation upon generation forever.
And they gave offense at Meribah Water, and Moses came to grief on their account
Because they had embittered his spirit and he spoke thoughtlessly with his lips.
They did not exterminate the peoples that Jehovah had told them to,
But mixed with the heathen and learned their doings
And worshiped their idols, and it became a snare for them,
And they sacrificed their sons and their daughters to the demons,
And shed innocent blood, the blood of their children Whom they sacrificed to the idols of Canaan, and the country was polluted with blood,
And they became unclean in their actions and unchaste in their behavior;
And Jehovah grew angry at his people and came to abhor his estate,
And gave them into the hands of heathens, and those who hated them ruled them,
And their enemies oppressed them and they were humbled under their hands.
Many times he delivered them, but they were disobedient in their conduct and moldered down in their guilt.
And he saw what distress they were in as he heard their appeal,
And remembered for them his covenant, changed his mind in accordance with the greatness of his friendship,
And made them objects of sympathy to all their captors.
Save us, Jehovah, our God, and gather us out of the nations To give thanks to your holy name, to glory in your praise.
Blessed be Israel’s God Jehovah from eternity to eternity. (And let all the people say Amen.)
Praise Jehovah! Thank Jehovah, because he is good, because his friendship lasts forever.
Let Jehovah’s rescued men say it, those whom he has rescued from the hands of a foe
And gathered out of many countries, from east and from west, from north and from sea.
Those who were wandering in the wilderness, in desert land, found no road to a city of homes,
Hungry, thirsty too, their souls in them fainting away,
But they cried out to Jehovah in their distress and he delivered them out of their hardships,
And set them on a straight course to go to a city of homes,
Let them thank Jehovah for his friendship and his wonderful deeds for mankind.
For he gives satisfaction to a hankering soul, and a hungry soul he fills with good things.
Those who were sitting in darkness and gloom, locked in misery and in irons,
Because they had disobeyed Deity’s word and despised the Most High’s advice
And he had humbled their hearts with trouble, they had stumbled and there was no helper,
But they cried out to Jehovah in their distress and he saves them out of their hardships,
Brings them out of darkness and gloom and breaks their chains,
Let them thank Jehovah for his friendship and his wonderful deeds for mankind.
For he smashes bronze doors and chops through iron bars.
Those who were sick because of their criminal course and in misery because of their guilt,
Their appetites abhorring any food and they nearing the gates of death,
But they cried to Jehovah in their distress and he saves them out of their hardships,
Sends his word and cures them and brings them clear of their blights,
Let them thank Jehovah for his friendship and his wonderful deeds for mankind
And sacrifice thank-offerings and shout the story of his deeds.
Those who have gone to sea in ships, done business on a great water,
They have seen Jehovah’s work and his wonders on the deep.
He spoke the word and a wind rose, a tempest that drove its waves high;
They go up to the sky, down to the depths, their souls rocking with disaster,
They dance and stagger like a drunken man and all their skill is at a loss.
But they have cried out to Jehovah in their distress and he brings them out of their hardships,
Turns a tempest to a hush; and the waves of the sea became still,
And they were glad that it calmed down; and he guided them to the port they wanted to reach.
Let them thank Jehovah for his friendship and his wonderful deeds for mankind
And exalt him where a people is assembled and praise him where elders sit.
He makes rivers into a wilderness and fountainheads of water into a thirsty spot,
A fruitful country into alkali soil, for the wickedness of those who live in it.
He makes a wilderness into pools of water and an arid country into fountainheads of water
And settles hungry people there, and they establish a city of homes
And sow fields and set out vineyards and are fruitful in produce,
And he blesses them, and they grow very numerous, and their cattle he does not make few.
And if they have become few and low by pressure of disaster and sorrow,
He pours contempt on nobles and sets them wandering in pathless nothingness,
But he uplifts a needy man out of misery and makes him into clans numerous as the sheep.
Upright men will see it and be glad, and all foul play shuts its mouth.
Whoever is wise, let him watch these things, and let them discern Jehovah’s deeds of friendliness.
(A song; a psalm of David’s.)
My heart is firm, God; I will sing and give praise.
Wake, my glory! wake, harp and lyre! I will wake the dawn.
I will give you thanks among the nations, Jehovah, I will make music among many a folk,
Because your friendliness is great to the skies and your loyalty to the uppermost air.
Abide aloft, God, above the sky, your glory above all the earth.
So that your darlings may be delivered save with your right hand and answer us.
God spoke in his sanctuary: “I will triumph, will divide Shekem, will measure off Succoth Vale;
Gilead is mine and Manasseh is mine, and Ephraim is the keep of my head; Judah is my baton.
Moab is my bathtub, on Edom I throw my sandal, over Philistia are my hurrahs.”
Who will bring me to a city for a siege? who has led me through to Edom?
Have not you, God, repudiated us? and you do not go out, God, in our campaigns.
Give us help from a foe— human salvation is futile.
Through God we shall play a sturdy part, and he himself will trample down our foes.
(Of the Director; of David’s; a psalm.)
God of my praise, do not be deaf,
For they have opened against me mouths of wrong and of treachery and spoken with me with tongues of falsehood
And encircled me with words of hatred and made war on me for nothing;
In return for my love they are adversaries to me; but on my part prayer.
And they have turned upon me evil in return for good and hatred in return for my love.
Give a wrong-doer authority over him and let an adversary stand at his right hand!
When he goes into court let him come out in the wrong, and let his prayer become sin!
Be his days few! let another take his station!
Be his sons orphans and his wife a widow,
And may his sons live as vagabonds and beg their bread and go out soliciting from the wasted sites they lodge in!
May a creditor bag everything he has, and strangers plunder the fruit of his toil!
May he have nobody that keeps up friendship, and his orphans nobody that shows them goodwill!
May his posterity come to extinction, their name be obliterated in another generation!
May Jehovah be reminded of his fathers’ guilt, his mother’s sin not be obliterated,
May they be always present to Jehovah and may he cut off their memory forever,
Since he did not remember to show friendship but hunted down a man wretched and needy and wounded to the heart, to give him his deathblow,
And loved a curse—so may it come upon him! and had no liking for a blessing—so may it be far from him!
And wore curses like his coat— so may they come into his inward parts like water and into his bones like oil,
Be to him like the clothing he is wrapped in and become the girdle he is always belted with!
These are the earnings due from Jehovah to those who are hostile to me and to those who are talking up evil against my life.
But do you, Jehovah, my Lord, take action on my side for the honor of your name, deliver me because your friendship is so good,
Because I am wretched and needy and my heart is stabbed within me.
I am gone like a lengthening shadow, tumbled out like grasshoppers.
My knees are giving way from fasting and my flesh has grown lean without oil,
And I have become a butt for their taunts, they see me and shake their heads.
Help me, Jehovah, my God, save me as befits your friendship,
That they may know that this is your hand, it is you, Jehovah, that did it.
Let them curse while you bless; let those who stand up against me be disappointed and your servant make merry.
Let those who are hostile to me be clothed in humiliation and wrapped in their shame as in a robe.
I will speak out great thanks to Jehovah and praise him in the midst of many
Because he stands at a needy man’s right hand to save him from those who would judge him for life or death.
(Of David’s; a psalm.)
Quoth Jehovah to my lord “Sit at my right hand till I make your enemies a footstool for your feet.”
Jehovah will send your strong staff out from Sion. Hold sway amid your enemies!
Your people come in willingly on your day of effort; on sacred mountains, from the womb of dawn, you have your dew of youth.
Jehovah has sworn, and will not revoke it, “You are priest forever on Malkisedek’s terms”;
The Lord is at your right hand. He has shattered kings on his day of anger;
He will give judgment among the nations; he has filled with bodies, has shattered heads over a great country.
He will drink from an arroyo on the road; therefore he will lift up his head.
Praise Jehovah! I will acknowledge Jehovah with entire heart in a council and company of upright men.
Great are Jehovah’s works, to be studied for all their charms.
What he has done is majesty and splendor, and his right-doing stands forevermore.
He did memorable wonders; kindly and tenderhearted is Jehovah.
He gave provisions to those who feared him, forever remembering his covenant.
He acquainted his people with the powerfulness of his workings, giving them the estate of nations.
The works of his hands are loyalty and justice; all his mandates are trustworthy,
Anchored forever and evermore, done in truth and rectitude.
He sent redemption to his people, ordained his covenant forever; holy and terrible is his name.
To fear Jehovah is the first thing in wisdom, good sense of all who exercise it; his praise stands forevermore.
Praise Jehovah! Happy a man who fears Jehovah, takes great pleasure in his commandments:
Eminent in the country shall his descendants be; a generation of upright men will be blessed.
In his house are resources and riches, and his rightness stands forevermore.
Light comes up in darkness for upright men; kindly and tenderhearted is a right-doer.
Good is a man who shows kindness and lends, keeps up his business in justice.
For he will be unshaken forever; an honest man will become an everlasting memory.
He will not be afraid at a report of disaster; his heart stands firm, trusting in Jehovah.
His heart is anchored; he will not be afraid till he gloats over his foes.
He has scattered, has given to the needy; his right-doing stands forevermore; his horn is carried high in honor.
A wrong-doer will see and be vexed, will grind his teeth and melt down; wrong-doers’ cravings will perish.
Praise Jehovah! Praise, worshipers of Jehovah, praise Jehovah’s name!
Be Jehovah’s name blessed from now to eternity!
From sunrise land to sunset Jehovah’s name is to be praised.
Aloft over all nations is Jehovah; above the sky is his glory.
Who is the like of our God Jehovah,
seated high, seeing low, in heaven and on earth;
Lifting the poor man from the dust, raising the needy man from the rubbish-dump,
To seat him with nobles, with the nobles of his people;
Making a barren woman a homemaker, a happy mother?
Praise Jehovah! When Israel came out of Egypt, Jacob’s family from a people of outlandish speech,
Judah became sacred to him, Israel his dominions.
The sea saw and took flight, the Jordan turned round backward,
The mountains leaped like rams, hills like sons of the flocks.
What happened to you, sea, that you should take flight? Jordan, that you should turn round backward?
That you should leap like rams, mountains, like sons of the flocks, hills?
Quiver, earth, before a Lord, before Jacob’s God,
Who turns the rock to a pool of water, a block of pyrite to a fountainhead of water.
Not to us, Jehovah, not to us, but to your name bring honor for your friendship and loyalty.
Why should the nations say “Where is their god?”
But our God is in heaven; he has done everything that he pleased to.
Their idols are silver and gold, work of human hands.
They have mouths and do not speak, they have eyes and do not see,
They have ears and do not hear, they have noses and do not smell,
Their hands, they do not handle; their feet, they do not walk; they do not whisper with their throats.
Like them be their makers, everybody that trusts to them!
Israel trusts to Jehovah; he is their help and shield.
The house of Aaron trusts to Jehovah; he is their help and shield.
Those who fear Jehovah trust to Jehovah; he is their help and shield.
Jehovah remembers us, will bless, will bless the house of Israel, will bless the house of Aaron,
Will bless those who fear Jehovah, the smallest with the greatest.
Jehovah add more to you, to you and to your sons!
Blessed be you of Jehovah, Maker of heavens and earth!
The heavens are Jehovah’s heavens, but the earth he has given to mankind.
The dead will not praise Jehovah, nor any who go down into silence;
But we will bless Jehovah from now on, forever! Praise Jehovah!
I love Jehovah, because he hears my suppliant voice,
Because he has bent his ear to me, and through my lifetime I will call.
The cords of death have enclosed me and the grip of the grave has caught me; I encounter distress and sorrow;
But on Jehovah’s name I call: ah, Jehovah, bring my life through.
Kind is Jehovah, and true to the right, and our God is tenderhearted.
Jehovah watches over simple people; I was poor, and me he saves.
Come back to your resting, my soul, because Jehovah has done you a good turn.
For you have rescued my life from death, my eyes from tears, and my feet from losing their hold;
I am walking before Jehovah in the lands of the living.
I believe while I speak; I have had a very hard time,
I have thought in my alarm “All men are shamming”;
What return shall I make to Jehovah for all his dealings with me?
I will lift a cup of salvation and proclaim Jehovah’s name,
Will discharge my vows to Jehovah in the presence of all his people.
Death for the men of his friendship is a serious matter in Jehovah’s view.
Ah, Jehovah, for I am your servant, I am your servant, your bondwoman’s son, you have unfastened my fetters.
To you I will sacrifice a sacrifice of thanksgiving and proclaim Jehovah’s name,
Will discharge my vows to Jehovah in the presence of all his people,
In the courts of Jehovah’s house, within you, Jerusalem.
Praise Jehovah! Praise Jehovah, all nations, laud him, every folk,
Because his friendship is supreme toward us and Jehovah’s loyalty lasts forever. Praise Jehovah!
Give thanks to Jehovah, because he is good, because his friendship lasts forever.
Let Israel say that his friendship lasts forever.
Let Aaron’s family say that his friendship lasts forever.
Let those who fear Jehovah say that his friendship lasts forever.
I called to Jehovah out of a tight pinch, Jehovah answered me in free range.
I have Jehovah for me; I will not be afraid; what is man to do to me?
I have Jehovah for me among my helpers, and I shall gloat over my haters.
Better to take refuge in Jehovah than to put confidence in man.
Better to take refuge in Jehovah than to put confidence in princes.
All nations have surrounded me— in Jehovah’s name I will stand them off.
Surrounded me they have, yes, surrounded me— in Jehovah’s name I will stand them off.
They have surrounded me like bees— they have gone out like a thorn fire, in Jehovah’s name I will stand them off.
You did give me a push to bring me down, but Jehovah helped me.
My strength and hymn is Jehovah, and he has been to me salvation;
In honest men’s tents there is a voice of shouting and victory: Jehovah’s right hand has done sturdily!
Jehovah’s right hand was swung high! Jehovah’s right hand did sturdily!
I shall not die but live and tell the story of Jehovah’s deeds;
Jehovah did chastise me, but did not give me up to death.
Open holy gates for me to go in by them, to praise Jehovah.
This gate is Jehovah’s; right-doers shall go in by it.
I thank you that you have answered me and been to me salvation;
A stone that the builders had rejected has become the head of a corner.
This was from Jehovah, it is a wonder to our eyes.
This day Jehovah has made; we will exult and make merry on it.
Ah, Jehovah, give victory! ah, Jehovah, give success!
Blessed in Jehovah’s name be he who is coming in; we bless you out of Jehovah’s house.
Jehovah is Deity and has given us light. Tie festival with cords clear to the horns of the altar.
You are my Deity whom I thank, my God whom I exalt.
Give thanks to Jehovah because he is good, because his friendship lasts forever.
Happy are men of conscientious course, those who go by Jehovah’s instructions.
Happy those who keep his lessons, wholeheartedly resort to him.
Neither do they commit knavery; they go by his courses.
It was you ordained your mandates, well to be observed.
Would that my courses were steady in observing your precepts!
I shall be then unashamed when I look toward all your commandments.
I will give you thanks with straightforward heart when I learn your righteous laws.
Your precepts I observe; do not totally leave me.
By what is a young man to keep his path clean? Watching it on the basis of your word.
Wholeheartedly I resort to you; let me take no wrong step away from your commandments.
In my heart I have buried your behest, so that I might not sin against you.
Blessed are you, Jehovah; teach me your precepts.
With my lips I tell the story of all the laws your mouth has given out.
In the course your lips teach I rejoice as much as over any affluence.
In your mandates I study, and eye your paths.
In your precepts I take my pleasure, will not forget your word.
Do your servant a good turn; let me live and observe your word.
Unblind my eyes and let me look at mysteries out of your instructions.
A visitor on earth am I; do not veil your commandments from me.
My soul wears away with wishing toward your laws at every time.
You rebuke presumptuous men; cursed are those who err from your commandments.
Roll off from me ignominy and contempt, because I keep your lessons.
If even chieftains sat talking together against me your servant would study in your precepts.
Your lessons are withal my pleasure, my advisers.
Flat on the ground lies my soul; give me life in accordance with your word.
I told my story and you answered me; teach me your precepts.
Give me insight into the course your mandates prescribe; that I may study your mysteries.
