My soul is dissolved in woe; set me on my feet in accordance with your word.
Turn away from me the course of falsehood and favor me with your instructions.
I choose the course of faithfulness, I crave your laws.
I have adhered to your lessons; Jehovah, do not disappoint me.
I will run the road of your commandments because you have set my heart at ease.
Instruct me, Jehovah, in the course your precepts direct, and I will keep it to the last.
Give me insight and I will keep your instructions and observe them wholeheartedly.
Direct me along the path of your commandments; for that is what I like.
Bend my heart toward your lessons and not toward pelf.
Lead my eyes to go past sights of frivolity; give me life by your word.
Make good to your servant your promise for the fear of you.
Drive off my ignominy of which I stand in fear, because your laws are good.
Here have I been wishing your mandates; give me life in your fairness,
And let your acts of friendship come to me, Jehovah, your salvation in accordance with your promise,
And let me give an answer to him who taunts me; for I am confident in your word;
And do not utterly cut off out of my mouth the word of truth, because I have been waiting for your laws,
And I will observe your instructions always, forever and evermore,
And walk a roomy road because I have betaken myself to your mandates;
And I will talk of your lessons in the presence of kings and never be ashamed,
And take my pleasure in your commandments which I love,
And raise my hands to your commandments, which I love, and study your precepts.
Remember for your servant your word, forasmuch as you are letting me wait.
This is my comfort in my misfortune, that your promise gives me life.
Presumptuous men have been very cynical to me— I did not swerve from your instructions;
I remembered your judgments since olden times, Jehovah, and took comfort.
I am seized with fever at wrong-doers who forsake your instructions.
Your precepts have been music to me in the house where I am on my visit.
I have remembered your name in the night, Jehovah, and observed your instructions.
This has been mine, that I have kept your mandates.
My portion is Jehovah; I resolve to keep your word.
I entreat you, Jehovah, with all my heart, be gracious to me according to your promise.
I thought over my courses and turned my feet back to your lessons.
I hastened and did not delay to observe your commandments.
Wrong-doers’ cords swing around me, I do not forget your instructions.
At midnight I stand up to give you thanks for your righteous judgments.
I am comrade of all who fear you, observing your mandates.
The earth is full of your friendliness, Jehovah; teach me your precepts.
You have done kindly by your servant, Jehovah, in accordance with your word.
Teach me good sense and knowledge, because I believe in your commandments.
Before I had my misfortunes I went wrong; but now I observe your behest.
You are good and do the good; teach me your precepts.
Presumptuous men have smeared lies over me; I keep your mandates with all my heart.
Their hearts are fatty as tallow; I take my pleasure in your instructions.
It was good for me that I had my misfortunes, in order that I might learn your precepts.
The instructions of your mouth are a better thing for me than thousands in gold and silver.
Your hands made me and organized me; give me intelligence and I will learn your commandments.
Those who fear you see me and are glad, because I wait for your word.
I know, Jehovah, that your judgments are right and it was in faithfulness you sent me misfortune;
Let your friendship come to comfort me in accordance with your promise to your servant;
Let your tenderness come in, that I may get well, because your instructions are my pleasure.
Let presumptuous men be ashamed that they have circumvented me with falsehood; I will study your mandates.
Those who fear you shall come back to me, and those who know your lessons.
Be my heart faultless by your precepts, so that I may not be put to shame.
My soul is spent with looking for your salvation; I wait for your word.
My eyes are spent with looking for your promise, thinking “How soon will you comfort me?”
Though I have become like a wineskin in a cloud of smoke, I have not forgotten your precepts.
How long is your servant’s time? how soon will you execute judgment on my persecutors?
Presumptuous men have dug pitfalls for me, men who do not conform to your instructions.
All your commandments are faithful; in falsehood they persecute me; help me.
They almost made an end of me on earth, but I did not abandon your mandates.
As befits your friendship give me life, and I will observe the lessons of your mouth.
Forever, Jehovah, your word stands in heaven.
To generation after generation your faithfulness lasts; you have set earth in order, and it stands.
For your laws they stand today; for everything is in your service.
If your instructions had not been my pleasure, then I should have perished in my misfortune.
Forever I will not forget your mandates, because by them you have given me life.
Yours am I; save me, because I have betaken myself to your mandates.
Wrong-doers have hoped to get me to destroy me; I seek insight into your lessons.
Of every thoroughness I have seen an end; your commandment goes far indeed.
How I love your instructions! they are my study all day.
Your commandment makes me wiser than my enemies, for it is mine forever.
I have more insight than all my teachers because I have your lessons as a study.
I am more sagacious than aged men because I keep your mandates.
From every vicious road I have shut off my feet in order to observe your word.
From your laws I have not turned off, because you have instructed me.
How delicious to my palate are your behest and promise, more so to my mouth than honey!
Out of your mandates I grow intelligent; therefore I hate every false road.
Your word is a lantern for my foot and light for my path.
I have sworn, and will make it good, to observe your just laws.
I am in great misfortune; Jehovah, give me life in accordance with your word.
Accept the outpourings of my mouth, Jehovah, and teach me your laws.
I carry my life in my hand all the time but never forget your instructions.
Wrong-doers have set a trap for me, but I have not strayed from your mandates.
I have your lessons as my estate forever, because they are the joy of my heart.
I have bent my heart to live up to your precepts to the last of all.
I hate undecided people but love your instructions.
You are my screen and shield; I wait for your word.
Away from me, evil-doers, that I may keep my God’s commandments!
Hold me up in accordance with your promise and let me have life, and do not disappoint me in my reliance.
Hold me firm, that I may be saved and take my pleasure in your precepts always.
You spurn all who go wrong from your precepts, because their duplicity is falsehood.
You have made an end of dross, all earth’s wrong-doers; therefore I love your lessons.
My hair stands on end for dread of you, and I am in fear of your judgments.
I have done what was lawful and right; do not leave me to those who deny me justice.
Be your servant’s bail for good; let presumptuous men not deny me justice.
My eyes are spent with looking for your salvation and for your righteous promise.
Do with your servant as befits your friendship and teach me your precepts.
I am your servant; give me intelligence to know your lessons.
It is time for Jehovah to act; they have violated your instructions.
Therefore I love your commandments more than gold, red gold.
Therefore I hold a straight course by all your mandates, I hate every false road.
Wonderful are your lessons; therefore my soul keeps them.
The doorway of your words shines out, giving good sense to simpletons.
I open my mouth and catch my breath because I am so eager for your commandments.
Face toward me and be gracious to me, as is right for those who love your name.
Make my footing sure in your behest, and let not any villainy dominate me.
Redeem me from man’s injustice, and I will observe your mandates.
Show your servant a shining face and teach me your precepts.
My eyes run streams of water for men’s not having observed your instructions.
Righteous are you, Jehovah, and just your laws.
You have ordained your lessons in righteousness and utter faithfulness.
My jealousy has consumed me because my foes have forgotten your word.
Fully sterling is your behest, and your servant loves it.
Insignificant and despised am I— I do not forget your mandates.
Your right dealing is righteous forever, and your instructions are truth.
Distress and hardship have befallen me; your commandments are my enjoyment.
Your lessons are right forever; give me understanding and I shall come to life.
I call with all my heart; answer me, Jehovah; I will keep your precepts.
I call you; save me and I will observe your lessons.
I am up in the twilight and clamorous, waiting for your word.
My eyes come up against the night watches studying in your behest.
Hear my voice in accordance with your friendship; Jehovah, give me life in accordance with your law.
Those who chase after enormity have come near; from your instructions they are far.
Near are you, Jehovah, and all your commandments are truth.
I know of old out of your lessons that you have laid their foundations forever.
See my wretched state and rescue me, because I have not forgotten your instructions.
Champion my cause and stand my friend; give me life as was your promise.
Far from wrong-doers is salvation because they have not betaken themselves to your precepts.
Your tenderness is great, Jehovah; give me life in accordance with your laws.
Many are my persecutors and foes; I have not swerved from your lessons.
I saw faithless men and was seized with loathing that they did not observe your behest.
See, because I love your mandates; Jehovah, give me life in accordance with your friendship.
The sum of your word is truth and all your righteous laws are forever.
Chieftains have been persecuting me without provocation, but it is of your word my heart stands in dread.
I rejoice in your promise as does one who finds great booty.
I hate and abhor falsehood; I love your instructions.
Seven times a day I praise you for your righteous laws.
Great peace have those who love your law, and nothing to stumble over.
I rely on your salvation, Jehovah, and live up to your commandments.
My soul observes your lessons and I greatly love them.
I observe your mandates and lessons because all my courses are before you.
Let my appeal come near before you, Jehovah: give me understanding in accordance with your word.
Let my plea come in before you; deliver me in accordance with your promise.
My lips shall pour out praise because you teach me your precepts.
My tongue shall sing of your behest, for all your commandments are right.
May your hand be for my help because I have chosen your mandates.
I am wishing your salvation, Jehovah, and your instructions are my pleasure.
Let my soul have life and praise you, and your judgments give me help.
I am astray like a lost sheep; look your servant up, because I have not forgotten your commandments.
(Song of the goings up.)
I have called to Jehovah in distress of mine, and he has answered me.
Jehovah, deliver my life from lip of falsehood, from tongue of treachery.
What shall he give you, and what give you more of, tongue of treachery?
A champion’s barbed arrows with live coals of broom-brushes.
Woe is me that I am away in Moshc, a denizen among the tents of Kedar!
My soul has had too much of living with those who hate peace.
I am peaceable; but when I speak they are for war.
(Song for the goings up.)
I raise my eyes toward the mountains; where is my help to come from?
My help is from Jehovah, maker of heavens and earth.
May he not give your foot up to slipping; may he who guards you not grow drowsy.
Not drowsy will he grow, nor go to sleep, who guards Israel.
Jehovah it is who guards you; Jehovah is your shade at your right hand,
By day the sun shall not strike at you nor the moon by night.
Jehovah will guard you from everything bad, will guard your life;
Jehovah will guard your going out and coming in from now to eternity.
(Song of the goings up; of David’s.)
I was gladdened by those who said to me “We will go to Jehovah’s house.”
Our feet are standing in your gates, Jerusalem,
Jerusalem, built like a city all linked together,
Where tribes go up, Jehovah’s tribes, A testimony of Israel’s, giving thanks to Jehovah’s name.
For there stand thrones for judgment, the thrones of David’s house.
Ask for Jerusalem’s peace! may those who love you prosper,
May there be peace over your common and prosperity in your palaces!
On account of my brothers and friends let me say “Peace be in you!”
On account of my God Jehovah’s house let me seek good for you.
(Song of the goings up.)
To you I raise my eyes, you who are enthroned in the heavens.
Lo, as servitors have an eye to their masters’ hands, a maid to her mistress’s, So our eyes are on our God Jehovah till he is gracious to us.
Be gracious to us, Jehovah, be gracious to us, for we have had the most we can take of contempt.
Our souls have had the most that they can take of ridicule by easy men, of contempt by proud men.
(Song of the goings up; of David’s.)
If it had not been for Jehovah that was on our side, let Israel say,
If it had not been for Jehovah that was on our side when man stood up against us,
Then they would have swallowed us alive in their anger against us;
Then the water would have swept us off, an arroyo flood have gone over our lives;
Then the blustering water would have gone over our lives.
Blessed be Jehovah, who did not give us up as prey to their teeth.
We feel like a bird that gets out of a fowler’s trap; the trap broke and we are out!
Our help is in the name of Jehovah, maker of heavens and earth.
(Song of the goings up.)
Those who put their confidence in Jehovah are like Sion mountain, unshakable, seated forever.
Jerusalem has mountains around her, and Jehovah is around his people from now to eternity.
For the scepter of wrong is not to rest over the lot of the righteous, in order that the righteous may not put their hands to disloyal work.
Do good, Jehovah, to good men and to men straightforward in heart;
But those who curve their devious course Jehovah will take along with the doers of villainy. Peace on Israel!
(Song of the goings up.)
When Jehovah came back to Sion we were like men in a dream.
Then our mouths were filled with laughter, our tongues with caroling; Then they said among the nations “Jehovah has done great things for these people!”
Jehovah has done great things for us; we have become merrymakers.
Come back to us, Jehovah, as it comes in gorges in the South.
Those who sow with tears will reap with carols.
The man carrying the seed for the planting goes along weeping, the man carrying his sheaves comes in with caroling.
(Song of the goings up; of Solomon’s.)
If Jehovah is not building a house its builders have taken useless trouble on it; If Jehovah is not guarding a city a guardsman has been uselessly vigilant.
It is useless for you when you get up early, do not sit down till late, Keep busy while you eat; he gives his loved ones the same in sleep.
Sons, now, are Jehovah’s allotting; the fruit of a wife’s body is a reward.
Like arrows in a champion’s hand, such are the sons of youthful years;
Happy the man who has filled his quiver with them. They will not come to grief when they speak with enemies in the gate.
(Song of the goings up.)
Happy anyone who fears Jehovah, goes by his roads.
You shall eat what your hands have toiled for; happy shall you be, and it shall be well with you.
Your wife shall be a fruitful vine in the back of your house, your sons like new-set olive-trees round your table.
Thus blessed shall be a man who fears Jehovah.
Jehovah bless you out of Sion, and may you look upon Jerusalem’s welfare all your lifetime
And see sons of your sons. Peace on Israel!
(Song of the goings up.)
Ever since my youth they have made plenty of assaults on me, let Israel say;
Ever since my youth they have made plenty of assaults on me yet could not master me.
Plowmen plowed on my back, plowed a long strip.
Jehovah, doer of right, has cut through wrong-doers’ rope;
All Sion’s haters come to grief and fall back,
Become like roof grass that dries up before it has made a stalk,
With which no reaper has filled his hand, no binder his arm,
And the passersby have not said “Jehovah’s blessing to you; we bless you in Jehovah’s name.”
(Song of the goings up.)
Out of deep gulfs I call to you, Jehovah.
Hear the sound, Lord, let your ears be sharpened to my suppliant voice.
If you kept watch of guilts, Lord Jehovah, who would stand?
But forgiveness dwells with you, so that you may be feared.
I hope in Jehovah; my soul hopes on his word.
I am waiting in soul for the Lord more than watchmen for morning.
Wait toward Jehovah, Israel, for with Jehovah dwells friendliness and much redemption with him,
And he will redeem Israel out of all his guilts.
(Song of the goings up; of David’s.)
Jehovah, my heart is not exalted nor my eyes lofty; I have not gone among great things and things too mysterious for me.
Verily I have soothed and stilled my soul. Like a weaned child in its mother’s arms, like the weaned child is my soul in me.
Wait toward Jehovah, Israel, from now to eternity.
(Song of the goings up.)
Remember for David, Jehovah, all his hardships:
That he swore to Jehovah, vowed to the Mighty One of Jacob,
“I will not go into my home, will not mount my bed,
Will give my eyes no sleep, my eyelashes no slumber,
Till I find a place for Jehovah, abodes for the Mighty One of Jacob.”
We heard of it in Ephrathah, found it amid Jaʽar’s wilds.
Let us go into his abodes, do reverence at the footstool of his feet.
Up, Jehovah, to come to your resting-place, you and your ark of might!
Let your priests be robed in righteousness and your godly men shout!
For the sake of your servant David do not refuse to listen to your anointed one.
Jehovah swore to David faithfully, will never go back from it, “Offspring of your body I will set on the throne for you.
If your sons keep my covenant and my lessons that I teach them You shall have their sons too sitting on the throne forevermore.”
For Jehovah chose Sion, wished it for his seat:
“This is my resting-place forevermore; here I will settle, because it I prefer.
Its provision of food I will bless and give its poor full meals,
And its priests shall be robed in salvation and its godly men shout aloud.
There I will have a horn grow for David; I have filled a lamp for my anointed one.
His enemies I will clothe in shame, and upon him my diadem shall bloom.”
(Song of the goings up; of David’s.)
Now what a good and charming thing it is when brothers do live together!
Like the good oil on one’s head, coming down over the beard, Aaron’s beard, that came down over the collar of his vestments,
Like Hermon dew, that comes down over Sion’s mountains; For there Jehovah ordained the blessing, life forever.
(Song of the goings up.)
O bless Jehovah, all you Jehovah’s worshipers who stand in Jehovah’s house of nights.
Raise your hands devoutly and bless Jehovah.
Jehovah bless you out of Sion, the Maker of heavens and earth.
Praise Jehovah! Praise Jehovah’s name, praise it, you Jehovah’s worshipers
Who stand in Jehovah’s house, in the courts of the house of our God.
Praise Jehovah because Jehovah is good, make music for his name because it is so delightful,
Because Jehovah has chosen Jacob for himself, Israel for his special reserve.
For I know that Jehovah is great, and our Lord beyond all gods.
Jehovah does everything he pleases in the heavens and on the earth, in the seas and all deeps,
Brings up vapor from the earth’s end, makes lightnings for the rain, brings out wind from his storehouses,
He who struck down the eldest sons of Egypt, man and beast,
Sent tokens and miracles in your midst, Egypt, on the Pharaoh and all his subjects;
Who struck down great nations and killed formidable kings,
King Sihon of the Amorites and King ʽOg of the Bashan and all the kings of Canaan,
And gave their country as an estate, an estate for his people Israel.
Jehovah, your name is forever; Jehovah, the remembrance of you to generation after generation,
Because Jehovah will pronounce judgment for his people and take pity on his servants.
The idols of the nations are silver and gold, work of human hands.
They have mouths and do not speak, they have eyes and do not see,
They have ears and do not give ear, there is no breath in their mouths either.
Like them be their makers, everybody that trusts to them!
House of Israel, bless Jehovah! house of Aaron, bless Jehovah!
House of the Levites, bless Jehovah! fearers of Jehovah, bless Jehovah!
Blessed be Jehovah out of Sion, he who dwells in Jerusalem! Praise Jehovah!
Give thanks to Jehovah, because he is good, because his friendship lasts forever.
Give thanks to the God of gods, because his friendship lasts forever.
Give thanks to the Lord of Lords, because his friendship lasts forever:
To him who has alone done great wonders, because his friendship lasts forever;
Him who made the sky with insight, because his friendship lasts forever;
Him who spread the earth over the water, because his friendship lasts forever;
Him who made great lights, because his friendship lasts forever,
The sun to rule by day, because his friendship lasts forever,
The moon and stars to rule by night, because his friendship lasts forever;
Him who struck the Egyptians in their eldest sons, because his friendship lasts forever,
And brought Israel out of their midst, because his friendship lasts forever,
With strong hand and outstretched arm, because his friendship lasts forever;
Him who cut the Red Sea in two, because his friendship lasts forever,
And took Israel across through the middle, because his friendship lasts forever,
But tumbled the Pharaoh and his troops about in the Red Sea, because his friendship lasts forever;
Him who conducted Israel through the wilderness, because his friendship lasts forever;
Him who struck down great kings, because his friendship lasts forever,
And killed august kings, because his friendship lasts forever,
King Sihon of the Amorites, because his friendship lasts forever,
And King ʽOg of the Bashan, because his friendship lasts forever,
And gave their country for an estate, because his friendship lasts forever,
An estate for his servant Israel, because his friendship lasts forever;
Him who remembered us in our lowness, because his friendship lasts forever,
And tore us out of the hands of our foes, because his friendship lasts forever;
Giver of bread to all mortals, because his friendship lasts forever;
Give thanks to the God of Heaven, because his friendship lasts forever.
By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat down, wept withal, when we remembered Sion.
Within it we hung our lyres on poplar trees,
Because there our captors asked us for words of song and our persecutors for merrymaking, “Sing us some of the songs of Sion.”
How are we to sing Jehovah’s song on foreign soil?
If I forget you, Jerusalem, may my right hand forget how to work!
May my tongue stick to the roof of my mouth if I do not remember, if I do not put Jerusalem higher than the peak of my happiness.
Remember Jerusalem’s day, Jehovah, for the sons of Edom, those who said “Clear it off, clear it off, to the foundation of it.”
Doomed daughter of Babylon, happy he who shall pay you back the treatment you have given us!
Happy he who shall take and dash out against the crags the brains of the children that play about in you!
(Of David’s.)
I will give you thanks, Jehovah, with all my heart, make music for you in presence of gods,
Do reverence toward your holy temple and give thanks to your name For your friendliness and loyalty, because you made your promise great beyond all your fame
On the day that I called out and you answered me, inspirited me, strength in my soul.
All earth’s kings shall acknowledge you, Jehovah, because they hear the words of your mouth,
And sing of Jehovah’s courses, because great is Jehovah’s glory.
For Jehovah is high and sees a low man, and knows a lofty man far away.
If I go through the heart of distress you will give me life, will reach out your hand against my enemies’ anger, And your right hand will save me;
Jehovah will carry through on my behalf. Jehovah, your friendship lasts forever; do not abandon the works of your hands.
(Of the Director; of David’s; a psalm.)
Jehovah, you have sounded me and know me,
you know my sitting down and my standing up, you far away are aware of what I have in mind.
You itemize my traveling about and my lying down to rest, and are familiar with all my courses.
When a word is not on my tongue, there you, Jehovah, know the whole of it.
You hem me in behind and before and lay your hand on me.
The knowledge is too mysterious for me; it is inaccessible; I am not capable of it.
Where shall I go from your spirit? and where shall I get away from your face?
If I go up in the sky you are there; and let me make my bed in the realm of death, there you are.
Let me lift the wings of dawn and alight at the back of the west,
Even there your hand will be leading me and your right hand grasping me.
And do I say “I will just have darkness shroud me and night enclose me,”
Even darkness does not make it too dark for you, and night is light as day; the darkness and the light are alike.
For it was you that built my vitals, were weaving me together in my mother’s body.
I acclaim you that you are fearfully mysterious; mysterious are your works, and my soul knows it well.
My bones were not unknown to you as I was made in secret, stitched in an underground place.
Your eye saw my germs, and they were all registered in your book; Many days they were shaped, and not one of them was lost.
And what a stupendous thing to me are the objects of your concern, Jehovah! how multitudinous is their sum!
I count them—they outnumber the sand; I make an end—I am still at you.
If you are killing a wrong-doer, God, and bloodstained men, turn aside from me;
Those who perversely disobey you, futilely set themselves up against you,
Do I not hate those who hate you, Jehovah, and loathe those who stand up against you?
I hate them with utmost hate; they have become enemies of mine.
Search me, Deity, and know my heart, test me and know my ideas,
And see if I have in me a course that leads to pain, and lead me on the course that lasts forever.
(Of the Director; a psalm; of David’s.)
Rescue me, Jehovah, from evil men, guard me from injurious men,
Who think of mischief at heart, are starting fights all day,
Have whetted their tongues like a snake’s, have under their lips an adder’s venom. (Selah)
Keep me out of wrong-doers’ hands, Jehovah, guard me from injurious men, who plan to give my feet a shove.
Proud men have buried a trap for me and persecutors have spread a net, on the roadside they have set snares for me. (Selah)
I have said to Jehovah “You are my God”; give ear, Jehovah, to my suppliant voice.
Jehovah, my Lord, might of my salvation, you have overarched my head when arms were busy.
Do not give what a wrong-doer hankers for; do not let his design work out. [Selah]
Those who surround me are lifting their heads against me; the mischief of their lips shall cover them,
Burning coals shall be dislodged upon them, he shall drop them into a fire, into pits where they shall not get up.
A man who depends on his tongue will not stand firm on earth; an injurious man evil shall hunt down stroke by stroke.
I know that Jehovah will execute sentence for a downtrodden man, justice for needy men.
Honest men shall indeed give thanks to your name, upright men shall be seated before your face.
(A psalm. of David’s.)
Jehovah, I am calling you; make haste for me; give ear to my voice as I call for you.
Let my prayer be made ready as incense before you, the lifting of my hands be an evening sacrifice.
Station a guard for my mouth, Jehovah, watch over the door of my lips.
Let my heart not incline to a bad thing, to find amusement in wrong-doing With villainous men, nor take a meal of their dainties.
Let a doer of right trounce me, let his friendship correct me; Let a wrong-doer’s oil not anoint my head, because they have fettered my prayer by their wicked acts.
Their judges are hurled down the sides of crags, and they shall hear my words, because they are pleasant.
Like clods torn open on the earth our bones are scattered as the world below would take them.
For my eyes are toward you, Lord Jehovah; I have taken refuge in you; do not let my life run out.
Guard me from the grip of the trap they have set for me and the snares of villains;
Let wrong-doers fall into its nets together while I pass through.
(Meditative; of David’s when he was in the cave; a prayer.)
Aloud to Jehovah I cry, aloud with Jehovah I plead.
Before him I pour out my complaint, before him I tell my distress,
While my spirit is failing; but you know my path. In the road that I walk on they have buried a trap for me.
I look on the right and see, and there is no one that takes an interest in me; My place to flee to is lost, there is no one looking out for my life.
I cry to you, Jehovah; I say “You are my refuge, my portion in the land of the living.”
Listen to my appeal, because I am in great want: Deliver me from my persecutors, because they are too strong for me.
Bring my life out of lockup to give thanks to your name; Honest men are awaiting my prospect that you will do me a good turn.
(A psalm of David’s.)
Jehovah, hear my prayer, give ear to my supplication, in your faithfulness answer me with your right-doing,
And do not take your servant into court, because no one living will be in the right before you.
For an enemy has persecuted my soul, beaten my life down to the ground, Seated me in places of darkness like men long since dead,
And my spirit has failed, my heart is aghast within me.
I remember ancient days, muse on all your doings, ponder the work of your hands.
I spread out my hands to you; my soul looks to you as does a country perishing with drought. (Selah)
Answer me quickly, Jehovah; my spirit has given out. Do not veil your face from me and have me be like those who are down in the Pit.
Let me hear of your friendship in the morning, because I am confident in you. Make known to me the road I am to go, because I lift my soul to you.
Deliver me from my enemies, Jehovah; to you I flee.
Teach me to do as is acceptable to you, because you are my God. Your spirit is good; let it lead me over level ground.
For the sake of your name, Jehovah, you will give me life; in your right-doing you will bring my soul out of distress,
And in your friendship you will annihilate my enemies and destroy all the assailants of my soul, because I am your servant.
(Of David’s.)
Blessed be Jehovah my Rock, who teaches my hands to do battle and my fingers to fight,
My friend and my fastness, my citadel and my own preserver, My shield and the one I take refuge in, he who treads down peoples under me.
Jehovah, what is man that you should know of him, a human being that you should think of him?
Man is like a puff of vapor, his days are like a passing shadow.
Jehovah, bend your sky and come down, touch the mountains and let them smoke.
Flash lightning and scatter them; send your arrows and throw them into confusion.
Reach your hand from above, free me and deliver me from deep water, from the hands of foreigners
Whose mouths speak hollowly and whose right hand is a hand of falsehood.
A new song let me sing for you, God, with ten-stringed lyre make music for you
Who give salvation to kings, who freed your servant David from baleful warfare.
Free me and deliver me from the hands of foreigners Whose mouths speak hollowly and whose right hand is a hand of falsehood.
That our sons are like young fruit-trees, grown tall in their boyhood; Our daughters like corner-posts carved in palace fashion;
Our barns full, giving out this sort and that; Our sheep lambing by thousands, by tens of thousands in our open spaces;
Our cattle loaded; no breached walls and no evacuations and no shrieking in our squares,—
Happy the people that has it like this; happy the people whose God is Jehovah.
(A hymn of David’s.)
I exalt you, my Divine King, and will bless your name forevermore.
Every day I bless you, and will praise your name forevermore.
Great is Jehovah and greatly to be praised, beyond exploration is his greatness.
Generation to generation shall laud your deeds and tell your feats,
Talk of the splendor of the glory of your majesty and study your wonders
And say the mightiness of your terrors, and I will tell the story of your greatness;
They shall pour out commemoration of the abundance of your goodness and shout your right-doing.
Kindly and tenderhearted is Jehovah, patient and great in friendliness.
Jehovah is good to everything, and his tenderheartedness is toward all his works.
All your works shall give thanks to you, Jehovah, and those that have your friendship shall bless you.
They shall utter the glory of your empire and speak your prowess,
Making known to mankind your feats and the glory of the splendor of your empire.
Your empire is an empire for all ages, and your dominion over every generation that comes. Jehovah is trusty in his words and friendly in all his deeds.
Jehovah is a supporter of all who are falling and a raiser of all who are bent down.
Every creature’s eyes look to you, Jehovah, and you give their food at the due time.
You open your hand and give your favor to satisfy every living thing.
Jehovah is fair in all his courses and friendly in all his deeds.
Jehovah is near to all who call on him, all who call on him sincerely.
He will do what those who fear him can welcome, and will hear their cry and save them.
Jehovah guards all who love him, but all wrong-doers he will root out.
My mouth shall speak Jehovah’s praise that all mortals may bless his holy name forevermore.
Praise Jehovah! Praise Jehovah, my soul;
I will praise Jehovah while I live, make music for my God while I exist.
Do not trust confidently in noblemen, in a human being to whom salvation does not belong:
The breath in him will go out, he will go back to the soil he came from, that day his goodwill is a total loss.
Happy he who has Jacob’s God for his help, whose reliance is on his God Jehovah,
Maker of heavens and earth, of the sea and everything in it; Him who keeps to loyalty forever,
doer of justice for those to whom it is denied, Giver of bread to hungry men; Jehovah undoes prisoners’ fetters,
Jehovah opens blind men’s eyes, Jehovah raises men who are bent down, Jehovah loves honest men,
Jehovah safeguards immigrants, Keeps orphan and widow on their feet and circumvents wrong-doers’ courses.
Jehovah shall reign forever, your God, Sion, to generation after generation. Praise Jehovah!
Praise Jehovah, because he is good; make music for our God, because he is sweet; praise is glorious work.
Jehovah is Jerusalem’s upbuilder, he collects the exiles of Israel,
He who heals men broken at the heart and bandages their aches,
Who counts off the stars, names them all.
Great is our Lord and supremely strong; his understanding is incalculable.
Jehovah keeps humble men on their feet, brings wrong-doers down on the ground.
Sing out to Jehovah in thanksgiving, make music for our God with a lyre,
Him who covers sky with clouds, who dispenses rain to the earth, who makes mountains grow grass,
Gives their feed to cattle, to ravens’ young as they call.
Not the pony’s mettle pleases him, not the man’s legs gratify him;
Jehovah is gratified with those who fear him, those who await his friendship.
Laud Jehovah, Jerusalem, praise your God, Sion,
Because he has strengthened the bars of your gates, has blessed your sons within you.
He who makes your domain prosperous, gives you your fill of the richest of wheat,
He who sends his behest on earth, right speedily does his word run;
He who gives snow like wool, scatters hoarfrost like ashes,
Throws his ice like scraps; before his cold who holds out?
He sends his word and melts them; he makes his wind blow, water trickles,—
Tells Jacob his word, Israel his rules and laws.
He has not done the like for any nation, and his laws they do not know. Praise Jehovah!
Praise Jehovah! Praise Jehovah out of the skies, praise him high aloft:
Praise him, all his angels, praise him, all his legions;
Praise him, sun and moon, praise him, all stars of light;
Praise him, sky of the sky, and waters above the sky!
Let them praise Jehovah’s name, because he commanded and they were created,
And he set them to stand forever and aye, set a rule that they were not to violate.
Praise Jehovah from the earth, sea monsters and all deeps,
Fire and hail, snow and black cloud, tempest-wind carrying out his word,
The mountains and all hills, fruit trees and all cedars,
The beasts and all cattle, reptiles and winged birds,
Earth’s kings and every folk, captains and all earth’s judges,
Young men, and maidens too, old men with boys!
Let them praise Jehovah’s name, because his name alone towers high, his majesty is over earth and skies,
And he has given a high horn to his people, praise to all the men of his friendship, To Israel’s sons, a people near to him. Praise Jehovah!
Praise Jehovah! Sing a new song for Jehovah, his praise in an assembly of men of friendship!
Let Israel be glad for his Maker, Sion’s sons jubilate for their King.
Let them praise his name with dancing, make music for him with tambourine and lyre,
Because Jehovah is looking graciously on his people, will make humble men magnificent in victory.
Let men of friendship exult in triumph, carol on their beds,
Acclamations to Deity in their throats and two-edged swords in their hands
To wreak revenge on the nations, punishment on many a folk,
Putting their kings in fetters, their aristocrats in iron shackles,
Executing on them prescribed justice; it is a glittering privilege for all the men of his friendship. Praise Jehovah!
Praise Jehovah! Praise Jehovah in his sacred place, praise him in the firmament of his might!
Praise Jehovah for his feats of power, praise him for his supreme greatness!
Praise him with blast of ram-horn, praise him with harp and lyre!
Praise him with tambourine and dance, praise him with sounding strings and pipe!
Praise him with loud cymbals, praise him with ringing cymbals!
Let all breath praise Jehovah; praise Jehovah!
The proverbs of Solomon the son of David, king of Israel,
For knowing wisdom and instruction, for understanding sentences of insight,
For getting instruction in the successful practice of honesty and justice and rectitude,
For giving shrewdness to simpletons, knowledge and practicality to a boy,
While a wise man hears and adds to his lore and an expert acquires technique;
For understanding proverb and paradox, wise men’s words and their riddles.
Fear of Jehovah is the first thing in knowledge. Wisdom and instruction ignoramuses despise.
Listen, son, to your father’s instruction, and never abandon your mother’s teachings,
Because they are a becoming garland for your head and a necklace for your throat.
My son, if sinners are inveigling you do not consent.
If they say “Come with us, let us lay an ambush for bloodshed, set a trap for an innocent man for nothing;
We shall swallow them alive like the grave, sound and whole like men going down to the world below;
We shall come across all sorts of valuable goods, fill our houses with booty;
You shall get an even split, we will have one purse for all,”
My son, do not walk on a road with them, keep your foot off their path,
Because their feet are running to evil and hurrying to shed blood.
For it is for nothing that the net flutters before the eyes of any bird,
And they are laying ambushes for their own blood, setting traps for their own lives.
Such is the fate of whoever grasps at gain; it takes its owners’ life.
Wisdom holloos on the street, sends out her voice in the squares,
Calls out at the crowded corners, says her say in the city at the gates,
“How long, simpletons, will you love simpleness, and cynics like to be cynical, and fools hate knowledge?
You should turn back at my admonition; I would stream my spirit for you, would make my words known to you.
Since I have called and you refused, held out my hand and nobody listened,
And you neglected my advice and would not have my admonition,
I on my part will laugh at your calamity, will make fun when what you dread comes,
When what you dread comes like a thunderstorm and your calamity arrives like a gale, when distress and hard straits come upon you;
Then they will call me and I will not answer, they will go in quest of me and not find me.
Inasmuch as they hated knowledge and did not choose the fear of Jehovah,
Would not have my advice, despised all my admonition,
They shall eat out of the fruit of their courses and have their fill out of their policies,
Because simpletons’ broken resolutions kill them and fools’ faith in their luck destroys them.
But he who listens to me shall dwell unafraid and be at ease from dread of harm.”
My son, if you take what I say and lay up my commands in your mind,
Giving a listening ear to wisdom and directing your heart to intelligence,
If you call up discretion and to intelligence you raise your voice,
If you hunt for it as you would for silver and search for it as you would for buried treasure,
Then you shall understand the fear of Jehovah and find the knowledge of God,
Because Jehovah gives wisdom; out of his mouth come knowledge and intelligence;
He lays away sensible ideas for the upright, shields those who walk conscientiously,
Protecting law-abiding ways and guarding the road of the men of his friendship;
Then you shall understand right and justice and fair dealing, every good line,
Because wisdom shall come into your heart and knowledge be delicious to your soul;
Good judgment shall guard you, intelligence shall keep you,
Delivering you from a bad course, from men who talk mischief,
Those who leave straightforward ways to go on roads of darkness,
Who are glad to do harm and exult in mischief to a friend,
Whose ways are crooked and they take dodging roads;
Delivering you from a stranger woman, a smooth-talking foreigner,
That leaves the mate of her girlhood and forgets the covenant of her god,
For her house is sinking to death and her roads run to ghosts—
Any who go in to her will never come back nor reach the ways to life,—
In order that you may walk in good men’s path and keep to honest men’s ways,
Because straightforward men will people earth and conscientious men remain in it,
But wrong-doers will be extirpated from earth and faithless men torn out from it.
My son, do not forget my instructions, but let your heart keep my commands,
Because they will add to your length of life, your years of health, and your welfare.
Let friendliness and loyalty never leave you, hang them round your neck,
And find favor and a reputation for judiciousness in the eyes of God and men.
Trust in Jehovah with all your heart and do not lean on your own expertness;
Along all your courses know him and he will keep your ways straight.
Do not feel as if you were wise; fear Jehovah and steer clear of what is bad;
It will be medicine for your navel and juice for your bones.
Honor Jehovah out of your means and out of the first of all your produce,
And have your barns filled with foodstuffs and your vats bursting with grape-juice.
Do not reject Jehovah’s discipline, my son, nor chafe at his correction,
Because it is the one Jehovah loves that he corrects and he hurts a son who is acceptable to him.
Happy a man who finds wisdom and a person who obtains intelligence,
Because it is a better bargain than silver, better revenue than hard gold,
It is worth more than coral and all your valuables are no equivalent for it.
It has long life in its right hand, riches and honor in its left.
Its courses are courses of delight and all its paths are prosperity.
It is bark from a tree of life for those who grasp it, and one who handles it is to be congratulated.
Jehovah laid the foundations of earth by wisdom, fastened up the sky by intelligence;
By his knowledge the deeps were laid open and the heavens shed dew.
My son, never let them get away from your eyes; keep sense and judgment;
They will make your life vital and your neck fine.
Then you will go your way confidently and your toe will not stub.
If you sit down you will have no dread; you will go to bed and your sleep will be sweet.
Do not be frightened at what simpletons dread, nor at the storm upon wrong-doers when it comes,
For Jehovah will be your reliance and guard your foot from getting caught.
Do not withhold a kindness from the one who might receive it when it is in your power to do it.
Do not say to your neighbor “Go along, come again and tomorrow I will let you have some” when you have some by you.
Do not cook up harm for your neighbor when he is living with you unsuspiciously.
Do not quarrel gratuitously with people if they have done you no harm.
Do not envy a rapacious man nor choose any of his courses,
Because a crook is a thing Jehovah detests but upright men stand on intimate terms with him.
Jehovah’s malediction is in a wrong-doer’s house, but honest men’s home he blesses.
He treats cynics in cynical fashion but favors the meek.
Wise men come in for glory, but disgrace makes fools conspicuous.
Hear, sons, a father’s tuition, and listen to knowledge of discretion,
Because I have given you good doctrine; do not abandon my instructions.
For I was a son of my father’s, a tender only child before my mother,
And he instructed me and said to me “Let your heart take up my words; keep my commands and live.
Get wisdom, get discretion; do not forget and do not deviate from the words of my mouth;
Do not abandon her but keep her; love her and she will guard you.
The first thing in wisdom is—Get wisdom! and pay all your assets for discretion.
Prize her and she will exalt you, she will bring you to honor when you embrace her.
She will give your head a garland of grace, will deliver to you a crown of grandeur.”
Hear, son, and receive what I say and it will make your years of life many.
I have directed you on the course of wisdom and set you on level roads:
In your walking your steps will not be cramped, and if you run you will not stumble.
Hold fast to discipline, do not let go; keep her, for she is your life.
Do not enter the path of wrong-doers nor tread the course of wicked men.
Disregard it, do not pass along it, sheer off from it and go past,
Because they do not get to sleep unless they have done something bad and are robbed of their sleep if they do not do an injury;
For they feed on wrong-doing for bread and drink outrages for their wine.
But right-doers’ path is like the rays of light, growing lighter and lighter till it is settled day.
Wrong-doers’ course is like murky gloom: they do not know what they will stumble over.
My son, listen to my words; bend your ear to my sayings;
Do not let them get away from your eyes; guard them in the core of your heart,
Because they are life for him who finds them and soundness for all his flesh.
Beyond everything that you take care of keep your heart, for out of it come springs of life.
Keep crookedness aloof from your mouth and shiftiness far from your lips.
Let your eyes look right onward and your gaze be directed straight before you,
See to the road for your feet and let all your courses be steady,
Do not turn off to right or left; Keep your feet aloof from what is bad.
My son, listen to my wisdom, bend your ear to my insight,
To be careful of sound judgment and have your lips keep knowledge;
For a stranger woman’s lips drip virgin honey and her throat is smoother than oil,
But her aftermath is bitter as wormwood, sharper than a two-edged sword.
Her feet are going down to death, she plants her steps in the world below.
That she may not heed the path to life, her roads wander about, she does not know how.
But now, sons, listen to me and do not deviate from what my mouth tells:
Make your course far from her, do not come near the door of her house,
For fear you should give your fortune to others and your years to a cruel man;
For fear strangers should consume your strength at will and your pains come into a foreigner’s house;
And in the sequel you should repent, when your flesh and muscle give out,
And say “How I did hate instruction and my heart despised admonition,
And I did not obey my preceptors nor bend my ear to my teachers!
I was within a tittle of coming to the utmost harm in the midst of assembly and congregation.”
Drink water out of your own cistern and the flow out of the middle of your own well.
Your fountains would scatter to the street, rills of water through the squares!
Let them be for you alone and nothing for strangers with you.
Be your springhead blessed, and have joy out of the wife of your youth.
Doe of love, ibex of grace, her breasts shall refresh you at every time, with love of her you shall be always maddened.
And why, son, should you be maddened with a stranger and embrace a foreigner’s bosom?
For a man’s courses face Jehovah’s eyes, who observes all the roads he takes.
His guilt will clutch him, the wrong-doer, and he will be caught in the cords of his sin.
Such a one will die for lack of discipline and run into ruin by his great ignorance.
My son, if you have gone security to another, have struck hands with a stranger,
You are trapped in the word of your lips, caught in the say of your mouth.
Do this, son, do, and deliver yourself, because you have got into the other man’s hand: go cringe to the other man and bluster at him.
Give your eyes no sleep, your eyelashes no slumber;
Break loose like a gazelle struggling out of toils or a bird out of a fowler’s hand.
Go to an ant, idler, see its courses and become wise:
It, that has no chieftain, marshal, nor ruler,
Lays in its food in summer, gets its provisions packed away in harvesttime.
How long will you lie abed, idler? when will you get up from your sleep?
A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding your arms to lie abed—
And your poverty shall come like a prowler and your want like a man under arms.
A reprobate, a villain, who quibbles,
Winks with his eyes, shuffles with his feet, makes signs with his fingers,
Has mischief in his heart, is working up harm every minute, sets quarrels going,—
Therefore his calamity will come suddenly, he will be incurably broken all at once.
Six things there are that Jehovah hates, seven that are detestable to his soul:
Lofty eyes, a false tongue, and hands that shed innocent blood,
A heart that frames plans of villainy, feet that run fast to what is bad,
A lie-blowing false witness, and one who sets quarrels going between brothers.
Keep your father’s command, my son, and never abandon your mother’s teachings;
Tie them over your heart always, string them round your throat.
When you walk it will guide you, when you lie down it will watch over you and you will wake up with it minding you.
For a command is a lamp and a teaching is light, and the admonition of discipline is a road to life,
To guard you from a ruinous woman, from the slipperiness of a foreign dame’s tongue.
Do not take inward pleasure in her beauty; let her not catch you with her eyelashes,
Because on account of an unchaste woman one comes down to a loaf of bread, and a man’s wife hunts dear lives.
Will a man take up fire into his arms and his clothes not burn through,
Or will a man walk on live coals and his feet not be burned?
So it is with him who goes in to another’s wife: nobody who touches her will go free.
They do not despise a thief, that he steals to fill his stomach because he is hungry;
But one who is found pays back sevenfold, gives all the goods in his house.
One who commits adultery with a wife lacks brains; it is a self-destroyer that does it.
He will get blows and dishonor, and his ignominy will be uneffaceable.
For jealousy is a man’s fury, and he will be unsparing on the day of revenge;
He will not take any composition-money into consideration, will not consent though you offer a high price.
My son, be careful of what I say and lay up my commands in your mind.
Be careful of my commands and live; and of my teaching as if of the apple of your eye.
Tie them to your fingers; write them on the tablet of your heart.
Say to wisdom “you are my sister,” and call discretion a relative,
To guard you from a stranger woman, from a foreigner that talks slippery language.
For I looked out of my house window, through my lattice,
And I saw among the simpletons, perceived among the youngsters, a brainless boy
Going along the street that went by her corner and stepping in the direction of her house
In the twilight, the evening hours, in the dead of night and the murky gloom;
And there coming to meet him was a woman with a prostitute’s rig and a close heart;—
Boisterous and wayward is she, her feet do not perch in her house;
Now in the street, now in the squares, and beside every corner she lies in ambush;—
And she caught hold of him and kissed him, said to him with a bold face
“I have welfare-sacrifices that must be eaten, I paid my vows today;
That was why I came out to meet you, to hunt up your face, and I have found you.
I have spread my couch with rugs, striped work of Egyptian yarn,
I have sifted myrrh, eaglewood, and cinnamon over my sofa.
Come on, we will quaff love till morning, have a gay night with endearments,
Because husband is not in the house, he is off on a long journey,
He took the moneybag with him; he will get home the day the moon is full.”
She swayed him with the thoroughness of her technique, tugged at him with the glibness of her lips—
He suddenly goes along after her like a steer coming to the slaughter, Or as a buck prances toward a decoy
till an arrow cuts open his liver; Like a bird’s hurrying into a trap and not knowing that its life is at stake.
Now, sons, hear me and listen to the words of my mouth:
Let your hearts not run off into her roads, do not stray along her paths,
Because she has stabbed down many and all her killed are a multitude.
Her paths are roads to the world below, going down to the chambers of death.
Is not wisdom calling and intelligence sending out her voice?
On the brows of wayside eminences, at crossroads she takes her stand;
At the sides of gates, at the entrances of towns, at the approaches to gateways she holloos
“To you, men, I call, and my voice goes to humankind:
Appreciate shrewdness, simpletons; fools, provide yourselves with brains.
Hear, for I will speak sound sense, and what my lips are opened for shall be correct,
Because my throat breathes truth and wrong is an abomination to my lips,
All that my mouth says is on the right side, there is nothing tricky and crooked in it,
It is all obvious to a man of understanding and plain to those who find knowledge.
Take my instruction and not silver— knowledge is preferable to hard gold;
For wisdom is a better thing than coral and all valuables are no equivalent for it.
I wisdom am neighbor to shrewdness and meet the knowledge of effective tactics.
The fear of Jehovah is the hate of what is bad; pride and pretentiousness and a bad course and a mischief-making mouth I hate.
Mine are sound policies and sensible ideas; I am discretion, mine is power.
By me kings reign and potentates prescribe the right;
By me generals command and nobles, all the judges of earth.
I love those who love me, and those who go in quest of me will find me.
Riches and honor I have on hand, goodly resources and a right-doer’s standing.
My fruit is better than hard gold, red gold, and the produce I reap is preferable to silver.
On a highway of right I walk, on midmost paths of justice,
Dispensing assets to those who love me and filling their coffers.
“Jehovah framed me first in line, foremost of his works in the past.
Of old I was constituted, at first before the origins of earth.
When there were no deeps I came to birth, when there were no springs, sources of water;
Earlier than mountains I was planted, before hills I came to birth,
When he had not made earth and open spaces and the multitudinous particles of the soil of the world.
When he fastened the sky I was there, when he arched a vault over the face of the deep,
When he braced the ether above, when he fortified the springs of the deep,
When he set his limit for the sea and water does not overstep his dictate, When he strengthened the foundations of earth,
I was master-workman at his side And was taking my pleasure day by day, playing before him at every time,
Playing with nature all over his earth, and my pleasure was among mankind.
And now, sons, listen to me— happy are those who keep on my courses.
Hear instruction and be wise, and do not neglect it.
Happy a man who listens to me, attent at my doors day by day, watching the jambs of my portal,
Because he who finds me has found life and obtained favor from Jehovah,
But he who sins against me is victimizing himself; all who hate me love death.”
Wisdom has built her house, has shaped her pillars seven,
Has killed animals for her meat, mixed her wine, set her table too,
Has sent her girls, calls out on the crests of eminences in the city
“Who is a simpleton? let him come this way; brainless? that I may say to him
‘Come, have some of my dinner and drink some of the wine I have mixed.
Leave off simpleness and have life, and tread the road of discretion.”’
—He who offers instruction to a cynic gets dishonor for himself, and he who admonishes a wicked man, it is his discredit.
Do not admonish a cynic, for fear he should hate you; admonish a wise man and he will love you.
Give to a wise man and he will be wiser yet; advise a right-minded man and he will add to his lore.
The beginning of wisdom is to fear Jehovah, and to know the Holy is discretion.
For by me your days shall be many and years of life shall be added to you.
If you are wise, you are wise for yourself; and are you cynical, you will carry the consequences alone.
Foolishness is boisterous; simplemindedness knows no shame;
And she sits at the door of her house, in a chair on eminences in the city,
To call to passersby, those who are treading their ways,
“Who is a simpleton? let him come this way; and brainless? that I may say to him
‘Stolen water is sweet and bread behind a screen is delicious’”—
But he does not know there are ghosts there; her guests are in the deeps of the realm of death.
The Proverbs of Solomon. A wise son gladdens a father, but a foolish son is misery to his mother.
A wrong-doer’s hoards do no good, but right-doing delivers from death.
Jehovah will not let a right-doer go hungry, but wrong-doers’ hankering he will balk.
He who does things with slack hand grows poor; but energetic men’s hands enrich.
A capable son is stowing things away in summer; a worthless son lies fast asleep in harvesttime.
There are blessings for a right-doer’s head, but outrage covers up wrong-doers’ mouths.
The memory of a right-doer is for a blessing, but wrong-doers’ names will decay.
A man of wise heart takes orders, but a man of ignorant lips makes trouble.
One who walks plainly walks safely, but one who tangles his courses will be shown up.
A winker gives woe, but an outspoken reprover brings soundness.
An honest man’s mouth is a fountainhead of life; but outrage covers up wrong-doers’ mouths.
Hate starts quarrels, but love covers over all offenses.
On an intelligent man’s lips wisdom is found; but a cudgel is the thing for a brainless man’s back.
Wise men keep knowledge under cover; but an ignorant man’s mouth is ruin close at hand.
A rich man’s goods are his strong city; the destitution of poor men is their ruin.
What a right-doer has worked on goes for life; a wrong-doer’s produce, for sin.
He who lives up to lessons is on a road to life, but he who ignores admonition is off the track.
Lying lips cover up hatred; but he who gives out scandal is a fool.
In multiplicity of words offense will not be lacking; but he who keeps his lips under restraint is acting sensibly.
An honest man’s tongue is sterling silver; wrong-doers’ brains are worth little.
An honest man’s lips shepherd many; but ignoramuses die by lack of brains.
Jehovah’s blessing is what makes one rich, and pains add nothing extra.
Committing enormity is just fun to a fool, and so is wisdom to an intelligent man.
What a wrong-doer stands in terror of is what will come to him; but honest men’s desire will be granted.
When a gale has gone past, a wrong-doer is not there; but an honest man is permanently fixed on his foundation.
As is vinegar to the teeth and as is smoke to the eyes, so is the idler to those who send him.
The fear of Jehovah adds days; but wrong-doers’ years will be shortened.
Right-doers’ prospect is gladness; but wrong-doers’ hope will be lost.
Jehovah is a citadel to a man of conscientious course but ruin to villains.
A right-doer will be unshaken forever, but wrong-doers will not have a lodgment in the country.
A right-doer’s mouth bears crops of wisdom, but a mischief-making tongue will be cut out.
A right-doer’s lips know courtesy, but wrong-doers’ mouths misbehavior.
Cheating scales are what Jehovah detests, and a full-standard weight is what he approves.
Comes pretentiousness, comes dishonor; but wisdom is on the side of modest men.
Straightforward men’s conscientiousness will guide them, but faithless men will be upset by their wickedness.
Property does no good on a day of wrath, but right-doing delivers from death.
A conscientious man’s rectitude will smooth his course, but a wrong-doer will fall by his tendency to wrong.
Straightforward men’s rectitude will deliver them, but faithless men will be caught by their greed.
At man’s death hope perishes and the prospect vigor gave is lost.
An honest man is rescued out of distress and a rogue goes in instead.
By an ungodly man’s mouth his neighbor is ruined, but by knowledge honest men are rescued.
When good things happen to honest men a town jubilates, but when rogues perish there is shouting.
By upright men’s blessing a town stands tall, but by rogues’ mouths it is demolished.
A brainless man despises his neighbor, but an intelligent man holds his tongue.
A tattler discloses confidences, but a man of trusty spirit covers a matter up.
By not having political skill a people falls; but preservation comes by plenty of advisers.
One comes to grievous harm because he has gone security for a stranger; but he who hates hand-strikers has nothing to fear.
A gracious woman holds honor, but a woman who hates the right things, a chair of dishonor. Idlers will lack means, but aggressive men will control riches.
A friendly man is befriending himself; but a cruel man is breeding trouble for his own flesh.
A wrong-doer makes illusory revenue, but he who sows the seed of right, real wages.
Firmness in the right makes for life; but one who chases after evil does this for his own death.
Men crooked in their hearts are what Jehovah detests, and men conscientious in their courses are what he approves.
Hand on hand a vicious man will not be cleared, but right-doers’ descendants escape.
A beautiful but wrong-headed woman is a gold ring in a hog’s nose.
Honest men’s desire is pure kindness, but rogues’ hope is truculence.
There is such a thing as one who scatters but has more and more; but one who scrimps unduly is headed only for want.
A generous soul will get plenty of oil, and a man who gives water freely, plenty of water for himself.
One who refuses to sell grain the people will curse, but there will be blessings for the head of one who does sell it.
One who goes after good is going to find God’s favor, and one who hunts for harm will have it come to him.
He who puts confidence in his riches, he will fall, but right-doers will bud out like leaves.
One who breeds trouble for his house will have an estate of air; and an ignoramus is slave to a man with a wise brain.
The fruit of right-doing is bark from a tree of life, but rascality takes lives away.
Here an honest man has a narrow margin of well-being— how much more a rogue and sinner!
One who loves being instructed loves knowledge; but one who hates being corrected goes stupid.
A kindly man will obtain favor from Jehovah, but a schemer he will condemn.
Man is not set firm by wrong-doing; but right-doers’ roots are unshaken.
A worthy wife is her husband’s crown, but a worthless one is like a rot in his bones.
Honest men’s plans are for legitimate procedure; rogues’ tactics are fraud.
Rogues’ words are an ambush for bloodshed, but upright men’s mouths deliver them.
Upset rogues and they are nowhere; but honest men’s house will stand.
A man will be praised in proportion to his good judgment; but a dizzy-headed man will come into contempt.
A nobody who owns a slave is better than a pretentious man short of bread to eat.
A right-minded man knows the wants of his animal; but vicious men’s feelings are brutal.
One who works his ground will have plenty of bread; but one who runs after unpractical things lacks brains.
Love for wrong-doing is a net for bad men; but honest men’s root is permanent.
In crime of the lips is a disastrous snare, but an honest man gets out of the pinch.
Out of the fruit of a man’s mouth he will have his fill of good, and the dealing of one’s hands will come back to him.
A know-nothing’s course seems all right to him, but he who listens to advice is wise.
A know-nothing’s pique is displayed on the spot, but a shrewd man covers up a dishonor.
Who utters reliable facts shows the right; but a false-speaking witness, a cheat.
There is such a thing as a man whose jabber is like sword-stabs; but wise men’s tongue is healing.
A lip of truth will stand fast forevermore, but a tongue of falsehood for an instant.
There is double-dealing in the hearts of those who are cooking up harm, but those who confer on wholesome policy have happiness.
No trouble will be brought upon a right-doer; but wrong-doers are full of evil.
Lips of falsehood are what Jehovah detests, but men who act truly are what he approves.
A shrewd man covers up knowledge, but fools’ hearts bawl ignorance.
Energetic men’s hands will have control, but slackness will come to servitude.
Worry in a man’s heart depresses it, but thinking of a good thing gladdens it.
A right-doer will hunt up his pasture, but the course wrong-doers are on will make them lose their way.
Slackness does not broil his game; but energy treats a man’s goods as worth caring for.
On the highway of right there is life, but an avenger’s course leads to death.
A wise son a father’s instruction, but a cynic hears not a rebuke.
Out of the fruit of a man’s mouth he will eat good, but faithless men’s appetite is for outrage.
He who keeps watch of his mouth is guarding his life; he who throws his lips open comes to ruin.
An idler has an appetite and finds nothing, but energetic men’s appetite will find plenty of oil.
An honest man hates a false word, but a rogue leaves you disappointed and abashed.
Right-doing keeps safe a man of conscientious course, but sin upsets wrong-doers.
There are such things as a man who makes himself out rich and there is nothing at all there, and a man who makes himself out poor and there are quantities of goods.
A man’s riches buy off his life; but a poor man hears not a rebuke.
Right-doers’ light is merry, and wrong-doers’ lamp goes out.
A man with nothing in him will start a squabble by self-will; but wisdom is with men who take advice.
Property got together in a rush will shrink; but one who gathers bit by bit will make much.
An expectation long drawn out breeds sickness in the heart; but a desire that comes true is bark from a tree of life.
One who despises a word will have to give security; but one who fears a commandment, he will go safe.
A wise man’s precept is a spring of life for keeping away from the snares of death.
Tact gives charm; but faithless men’s course is to perdition.
Any shrewd man acts by knowledge; but a fool spreads out ignorance.
An unscrupulous messenger tumbles one into disaster, but a trustworthy courier is healing.
Poverty and dishonor, who neglects instruction; but one who observes admonition will come to high standing.
A desire realized is sweet to the soul; but avoiding anything bad is what fools detest.
Go with wise men and become wise; but one who cultivates fools will come to harm.
Disaster pursues sinners, but comfortable prosperity rests with honest men.
A good man will bequeath an inheritance to children’s children, but a sinner’s wealth is stored away for an honest man.
Plenty of food, poor men’s sod-breaking; but there is such a thing as one that is swept away without justice.
He who holds back his stick hates his son, but he who loves him goes in quest of it as a discipline.
A right-doer eats all his appetite wants, but wrong-doers’ stomachs are scrimped.
Women’s wisdom builds its house, but foolishness is demolishing it with her own hands.
He who fears Jehovah goes straightforwardly, but he who despises him takes dodging courses.
In a know-nothing’s mouth there is a switch for his own back, but wise men’s lips guard them safe.
With no cattle there is a clean manger, but there is plenty of produce by a horned beast’s strength.
A trustworthy witness will not lie, but a false witness breathes lies.
A cynic hunts for wisdom and does not find any, but knowledge is an easy thing to a man of sense.
Go face to face with a foolish man, and you have not known lips of knowledge.
A shrewd man’s wisdom consists in understanding his course; but the stupidity of fools, in cheating.
Reprobates’ homes are held guilty, but upright men’s houses are accepted.
A heart knows its own grief, and a stranger does not mix in its gladness.
Wrong-doers’ house will be rooted out, but upright men’s home will bloom.
There is such a thing as a road that lies smooth before a man but the last part of it is the recesses of death.
Even in laughter a heart will feel pain, and the sequel of gladness is sorrow.
A man of recreant heart will have his fill out of his courses, and a good man out of his practices.
A simpleton believes every word, but a shrewd man considers his steps.
A wise man is afraid and gets out of the way of harm, but a fool is hotheaded and confident.
A quick-tempered man acts foolishly, but a practical man bears.
Simpletons come in for an estate of ignorance, but shrewd men crown themselves with knowledge.
Bad men are brought low before good men and wrong-doers are at a right-doer’s gates.
A poor man is hateful even to his friend; but there are many to love a rich man.
One who despises his neighbor is sinning, but happy is he who shows favor to poverty-stricken men.
Practitioners of evil are on the wrong track indeed, but practitioners of good work in friendship and loyalty.
By any hard work there will be a clear profit; but lip-talk comes only to a deficit.
Wise men’s crown is shrewdness, but fools’ garland is foolishness.
A true witness is a lifesaver, but a lie-blower is a disappointment.
In the fear of Jehovah is a strong reliance, and to one’s children that will be a refuge.
The fear of Jehovah is a spring of life for keeping away from the snares of death.
In the numerousness of a people is a king’s majesty, but in lack of folk is a potentate’s ruin.
A patient man shows great intelligence, but an impatient man conspicuous foolishness.
A placid heart is life in the flesh, but passion is a rot in the bones.
One who denies a poor man his rights is insulting him who made him; but he who is honoring him shows favor to a needy one.
A rogue is knocked over by his viciousness, but an honest man finds refuge in his conscientious life.
In a sensible man’s heart wisdom rests, but in fools’ bosoms it is known.
Right-doing uplifts a nation, but sin is a disgrace to any folk.
A capable official will have a king’s approval, but a worthless one will be his rage.
A soft answer wards off ill temper, but a harsh word brings up anger.
Wise men’s tongues know what is what, but fools’ mouths stream ignorance.
Jehovah’s eyes are in every place, keeping a lookout over bad men and good.
Calmness of tongue is bark from a tree of life, but upsetting in it means a fracture in the spirit.
A know-nothing is contemptuous of his father’s training, but one who observes admonition will grow shrewd.
A right-doer’s house has in it plenty of capital; but in a wrong-doer’s produce trouble breeds.
Wise men’s lips sprinkle knowledge, but fools’ hearts are not right.
Wrong-doers’ sacrifice is what Jehovah abominates, but upright men’s prayer is what he accepts.
What Jehovah abominates is a wrong-doer’s course; but a pursuer of right he loves.
A path-leaver gets hard discipline; a hater of admonition will die.
The world of the dead, the land of the gone forever, are present before Jehovah; much more the hearts of human beings.
A cynic does not love being admonished; he does not go to wise men.
A glad heart does good to the face; but with pain at heart comes a broken-down spirit.
A sensible heart hunts up knowledge, but fools’ mouths pasture on ignorance.
All a doleful man’s days are bad, but a cheery man is a banquet all the time.
Better a little in the fear of Jehovah than a great store and everything going wrong in it.
Better a dish of greens when love is there than a stall-fed cow and hate about it.
A hot-tempered man sets quarrels going, but a patient man quiets a dispute down.
An idler’s path is like a thorn hedge; but downright men’s route is a made road.
A wise son gladdens a father, but a fool despises his mother.
Foolishness is bliss to a brainless man, but an intelligent man will go straight.
Frustration of plans comes by not going into conference, but by plenty of advisers they will go through.
A man enjoys having given a pat answer; and what a good thing a well-timed word is!
A canny man holds an upward path to life, to shun the realm of death below.
Jehovah sweeps off proud men’s house, but sets in place a widow’s boundary-mark.
A bad man’s ideas are what Jehovah detests, but pure men’s say is delightful.
One who grasps at gain is breeding trouble for his house, but one who hates gifts will live.
A right-doer’s heart studies to give an answer, but wrong-doers’ mouths stream viciousness.
Jehovah is far from wrong-doers but hears right-doers’ prayer.
Shining eyes gladden a heart, and good news puts fat in one’s bones.
An ear that can hear admonition is life; it will harbor itself amid wise men.
One who neglects instruction thinks nothing of his own being; but one who listens to admonition is getting brains.
Fear of Jehovah is a discipline in wisdom, and humility is antecedent to dignity.
Man’s are cogitations of the heart, but from Jehovah is the answer for the tongue.
A man feels as if all his courses were irreproachable, but Jehovah gauges spirits.
Turn your affairs over to Jehovah and have your plans confirmed.
Jehovah made everything to play its part, and even a wrong-doer for a day of disaster.
Any pretentious man is what Jehovah detests; hand on hand he will not be cleared.
By friendliness and loyalty guilt is purged, and by fearing Jehovah one avoids what is bad.
When Jehovah approves a man’s courses he makes even his enemies live on good terms with him.
Better a little by right than a large income by injustice.
Man’s heart plans his course but Jehovah places his steps.
Clairvoyance sits on a king’s lips; in giving judgment his mouth will not play false.
Steelyard and scales are matter for Jehovah’s judgment; all standard weights are his work.
The doing of wrong is a thing kings abominate, because it is by right that a throne is made firm.
Right-speaking lips are what a king approves, and one who speaks straightforwardly he loves.
A king’s ire means messengers of death, and a wise man will appease it.
In cheerfulness on a king’s face there is life, and his approval is like a spring rain-cloud.
Get wisdom; how much better it is than hard gold! and getting discretion is preferable to silver.
Avoidance of evil is straightforward men’s highway; he who watches his course is guarding his life.
Pride goes before a crash and a pretentious spirit before a tumble.
Better lowliness of spirit in humble men’s company than dividing booty with proud men.
One who handles a matter cannily will have good results; but one who trusts in Jehovah, happy he!
A wise-hearted man will be called a sage, but pleasingness of lips will add to influence.
The insight of those who have insight is a fountain of life, but ignoramuses’ lecturing is ignorance.
A wise man’s heart makes his mouth skillful and adds to the influence of his lips.
Pleasant words are a comb of honey, sweetness for the palate and health for the bones.
There is such a thing as a road that lies smooth before a man but the last part of it is the recesses of death.
A hardworking man’s appetite works for him, because his mouth sees to his working.
A reprobate is a furnace of harm and has on his lip what is like a searing fire.
A mischief-maker starts quarrels and a scandalmonger alienates a bosom friend.
A scoundrel inveigles his friend and makes him take a course there is no good in.
One who shuts his eyes tight is thinking up mischief; one who moves his lips has got up something bad.
White hair is a magnificent coronet; it will be found by a course of right-doing.
A patient man is better than a champion fighter, and one who has command over his spirit than one who takes a city.
The lot is tossed in the fold of your mantle, but every decision it gives is from Jehovah.
Better a dry morsel and a quiet life by it than a house full of dinner from ill-will sacrifices.
A capable slave will have control over a worthless son and will share inheritance among brothers.
Crucible for silver and furnace for gold, but he who assays hearts is Jehovah.
He is a malefactor who listens eagerly to a villainous lip; it is falsehood that gives ear to a malignant tongue.
One who jeers at a poor man is insulting him who made him; one who is glad at calamity will not be held innocent.
Grandchildren are old men’s coronet; but sons’ adornment is their fathers.
A grandiloquent lip is not becoming to a rascal; much less a falsifying lip to a noble.
A bribe shows itself to its user as a favor-charm: whatever he faces toward, he succeeds.
One who is looking for love covers up an offense; but one who harps on a matter alienates a bosom friend.
A rebuke sinks deeper into a man of sense than a hundred cuts with a stick into a fool.
A bad man seeks merely insubordination, and will have a cruel messenger let loose on him.
Let a man encounter a bear that has lost her cubs but not a fool in his ignorance.
One who returns bad for good will never have his house without bad.
The beginning of a quarrel is somebody letting a trickle start, so give up your side of the dispute before anybody gets into a rage.
One who declares a man right when he is wrong and one who declares him wrong when he is right are both of them things that Jehovah detests.
Why should a fool have in his hands a fee to buy wisdom when he has no brains?
The friend loves at every time, but a brother is born for distress.
A brainless man strikes hands, pledges a security before another.
One who loves a squabble loves a bruise; one who makes his doorway tall is asking for a crash.
A man with a crooked heart will come to no good, and a man with a reversible tongue will fall into disaster.
To one who begets a fool it becomes a sorrow, and a rascal’s father will not be glad.
A glad heart gives good healing, but a broken-down spirit dries out a bone.
A bribe is taken out of a rogue’s pocket to warp the courses of justice.
Wisdom is face to face with a man of sense, but a fool’s eyes are at earth’s end.
